detail.abstract:
The Human Capital Bond™ (HCB™) is the inevitable evolution of institutional impact
investing: the first fixed income instrument specifically designed to price human cognitive
capital appreciation in the AI economy, and the financial architecture required to operationalise
the recommendations of the Milburn Review (May 2026). Where impact capital has remained
a concessionary niche, the HCB™ brings social and actuarial outcomes into the core fixed-
income allocation through a standardised, rated, automated coupon. Issued by a bankruptcy-
remote Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) against a verified cohort of HSAS™-assessed
workers, the HCB™ provides institutional investors with a fixed coupon plus a variable Early
Detection Dividend™ (EDD™) uplift across four tranches: Tranche A (Category 3 appreciating
cohort, AAA equivalent, SONIA + 45bp); Tranche B (Category 2 augmented stable cohort, A
equivalent, SONIA + 95bp); Tranche C (Category 2 boundary cohort, BB equivalent, SONIA
+ 185bp); and Tranche D (neurodivergent Category 3 cohort, NWF Social Impact, SONIA +
55bp).
Unlike a traditional Social Impact Bond (SIB) — criticised for sub-scale issuance, bespoke
contracting, illiquidity and contested outcome attribution — the HCB™ converts verified social
and actuarial outcomes into a standardised, rated, automated coupon. The EDD™ is paid
when independently verified early HSAS™ assessment prevents Category 2→1 migration,
extends a Category 3 career, or achieves a Milburn Review™ neurodivergent NEET-
prevention outcome. This version (V2) closes the institutional gaps identified by an NWF
investment committee, an LGPS trustee board, a rating agency and a regulator. It specifies: a
three-layer EDD™ verification architecture with a conflict-of-interest firewall and binding
dispute resolution; a fully articulated SPV cashflow waterfall with reserves, coverage ratios,
amortisation triggers and a default definition; a rating-agency methodology grounded in the
cohort principle; anti-manipulation and fraud-prevention clauses; an ESRS S1 assurance
mechanism; and dedicated Market Failure, Regulatory Pathway and Risk Factors
sections. The proprietary telemetry components (HSAS™, PAQOS™, QFI™, CDP™) are
presented as Standardized Telemetry Components to support the auditability institutional
investors require. This paper is released as a working paper on SSRN to establish intellectual
priority.

title: Process Automation as a Market Entry Enabler: How Polish SMBs Adopt No-Code Applications to Support B2B Scaling
affiliations: University of Warsaw

detail.title: Process Automation as a Market Entry Enabler: How Polish SMBs Adopt No-Code Applications to Support B2B Scaling
detail.abstract: Foreign firms entering the Polish B2B market typically frame their challenge in commercial terms: how to generate leads, qualify prospects, and close deals in an unfamiliar cultural and linguistic environment. This article argues that the challenge has an equally important operational dimension that is systematically underestimated: the degree to which a target company's internal processes are digitally mature enough to absorb a new supplier's product. Drawing on macroeconomic data from Eurostat (2024, 2025), the European Commission's Digital Decade Country Report for Poland (2024), KPMG's Business Digital Transformation Monitor (2023), and a series of documented no-code implementation case studies from Polish SMBs — including projects delivering savings of 600 working hours annually and reductions in client onboarding time of up to 68% (Digital Development, 2025a; Digital Development, 2025b) — the article develops the concept of operational readiness as a structural variable in the B2B purchasing decision. It further examines the no-code and low-code platform market as both a symptom of and a solution to the digitalization gap in Polish SMBs, and considers the implications for foreign technology providers seeking to enter Poland. The findings suggest that the penetration of no-code tools among Polish service-sector firms is simultaneously creating a new addressable market for B2B software and increasing the pace at which Polish buyers can evaluate, trial, and integrate external solutions. For a practitioner overview of the Polish B2B market landscape, see also Wantuch (2026) and Piechota (2026).

detail.abstract: The AI Sovereign Liability Index™ (ASLI™) is the first benchmark reference rate for AI-driven human capital displacement risk. It constructs an eight-sector composite of human capital displacement velocity, weighted by sectoral exposure of the insured workforce, producing a single index score calibrated to the 95th percentile VaR reference rate. The index formula, input data waterfall, calculation agent specification, settlement rulebook, dispute resolution procedure, and IOSCO compliance framework are fully specified in this paper. This is the governance layer that makes a displacement number tradeable: it gives a pension fund trustee, an ILS desk, a reinsurer, and a regulator a common instrument with a legal settlement procedure. It is the longevity swap equivalent for labour income displacement risk — a risk class that pension funds, life insurers, private credit books, and municipal bond issuers currently carry with no hedge instrument available. The ASLI™ benchmark provides the reference rate those instruments settle on. This paper is released as a working paper on SSRN to establish intellectual priority and invite scholarly critique prior to regulatory and commercial engagement.

title: The Dark Tetrad in Entrepreneurship: Evidence from a General Population Sample
affiliations: University of Nevada, Reno - College of Business Administration - Department of Economics, University of Portsmouth and Tilburg University

detail.title: The Dark Tetrad in Entrepreneurship: Evidence from a General Population Sample
detail.abstract: This study examines the relationships between the Dark Tetrad personality traits-Machiavellianism, narcissism, psychopathy, and everyday sadism-and entrepreneurial outcomes, including intention, activity, and performance. Based on a randomly drawn general population sample, the results indicate that narcissism and psychopathy predict entrepreneurial intention. We do not find evidence for the hypothesized inverted U-shaped relationship between the Dark Tetrad and entrepreneurial performance. Our findings partially support the domination theory, suggesting that narcissism is associated with entrepreneurial intention due to domination rather than emancipation motives.

title: The Wisdom Premium: Senior-Biased Technological Change in the Age of AI

detail.title: The Wisdom Premium: Senior-Biased Technological Change in the Age of AI
detail.abstract: This paper documents a higher-level reallocation in recruitment patterns following the spread of the Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI). Using cross-disciplinary variation in AI exposure and applying a Difference-inDifferences strategy to administrative recruitment records of the Spanish Public Employment Service (SEPE) covering 2021-2025, I find that occupations with higher GenAI exposure experience a sustained increase in the share of new workers (over 50 years old) to 5.05 percentage points by 2025. This effect, which I call the Wisdom Premium, is strongly geared towards qualifications: it is almost entirely driven by high-level workers with postgraduate qualifications (Master's or PhD), whose hiring share grow by 3.70 pp, while professionals with lower education levels do not show any equivalent relative gains. The effect is distributed symmetrically across sexes and is concentrated in small and medium-sized enterprises, which represent the vast majority of the business landscape. These conclusions suggest that GenAI transforms accumulated experience and advanced training into a critical economic supplement, shifting the basis of the advantage of the labour market from task implementation to evaluative judgment. In older economies, where experienced workers have traditionally been considered vulnerable to technological displacement, GenAI can expand its productive relevance instead.

title: Health Insurance and Entrepreneurship in the US: A Structural Analysis
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania, School of Arts & Sciences, Department of Economics, Students

detail.title: Health Insurance and Entrepreneurship in the US: A Structural Analysis
detail.abstract: This study evaluates the impact of the US employer-sponsored health insurance system on entrepreneurship. The bundling of insurance and employment may discourage business creation by directly threatening potential entrepreneurs’ own coverage and by indirectly inflating hiring costs through compensating differentials for small firms that lack the scale to provide benefits efficiently, with the latter channel largely ignored in the existing literature. To quantify these forces, I estimate an equilibrium life-cycle model with occupational choice, insurance choice, benefit provision, and segmented labor markets. Counterfactual simulations of policies that decouple insurance from employment, such as the Affordable Care Act or universal public coverage, show that improved insurance portability encourages entrepreneurship and generates broad welfare gains through both channels. The results also suggest that policy-makers should target the indirect channel and small-firm employees beyond existing policies.

title: National Artificial Intelligence Economy Resilience Model: Structural Demand Failure in the AI Economy: A First-Principles Policy Response

detail.title: National Artificial Intelligence Economy Resilience Model: Structural Demand Failure in the AI Economy: A First-Principles Policy Response

declarations.funderStatement: This work internally funded as an economic modeling project by JWBA, Inc. James W. Bunger, Ph.D. President

detail.abstract:
Abstract

Artificial intelligence is raising the value of cognitive work at a historically unprecedented pace, and its promise is real: greater efficiency and broad prosperity. Yet that same acceleration is already displacing human labor from the production of this output. Left unmitigated, the commensurate loss of labor income carries a structural consequence — failure of the economy's demand circuit.

Human labor income recirculates to aggregate demand at a Marginal Propensity to Consume of 0.85; machine income recirculates at a Machine Marginal Propensity to Invest of 0.35. As AI displaces labor income with machine income at scale, the economy’s demand multiplier collapses. Productive capacity accumulates but buyers’ purchasing power does not. Prior technology transitions resolved this tension through net new job creation over 20-year horizons or longer. The AI S-curve’s characteristic displacement time is approximately 12 years — faster than any prior self-correction mechanism has operated.

Current policy responses — redistribution, deficit spending, monetary accommodation — address symptoms without engaging the circuit failure. Each of these levers is currently near saturation. None contains a mechanism that scales with the forthcoming displacement it is attempting to offset.

The National AI Economy Resilience Model (NAIERM) addresses the structural circuit failure through two integrated instruments: a Token Tax on AI compute services and a Participation Capital disbursement that channels that revenue into consumer demand at the high-MPC rate. Participation Capital is universal and unconditional — paid to every adult citizen regardless of employment or income status — and its amount is optimized in real time to economic conditions. The model is grounded in observed Bureau of Economic Analysis economic data, indexed to Q4 2025, and stress-tested across two displacement scenarios spanning 20 to 35 percent maximum workforce displacement.

The base case projects NAIERM GDP reaching $62.1 trillion by 2057 against a legacy trajectory of $44.6 trillion — a $17.5 trillion structural advantage. Productive capacity utilization of the legacy case falls from 81 percent in 2027 to 60 percent by 2040, meaning $26.1 trillion of annual productive capacity sits idle for lack of buyers. NAIERM maintains utilization at 77 to 91 percent throughout. The constitutional circuit surplus retires the federal debt by 2057, while Participation Capital displaces means-tested welfare, rendering it structurally obsolete by the early 2030s. The core finding is that all stakeholders — government, business and industry, and individuals — have a direct financial interest in the NAIERM circuit functioning.

title: Swap Curve Construction and Optimization of the Tension Parameter: An Energy-Partition Formulation
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Swap Curve Construction and Optimization of the Tension Parameter: An Energy-Partition Formulation

declarations.ethicsApproval: This is an original work which is based on my class project I did at Stevens Institute of technology in 2013 as part of MS in Financial Engineering. IO have expanded on my ideas and have used AI including Gen AI (Anthropic Claude) to build this paper.,

detail.abstract: Polynomial splines have long been used for the construction of swap curves. They suffer, however, from excessive convexity, a lack of locality under perturbation of the input rates, and the possibility of negative implied forwards. Tension splines remedy these defects through a single shape parameter, but the choice of that parameter has remained largely heuristic. In this paper we place the tension spline on its proper physical footing as the equilibrium shape of a thin elastic beam held under longitudinal tension, and we derive in closed form the two energies stored by such a beam: a flexural (bending) energy and an axial (tension) energy. We show that the curvature "smoothness" norm used in the literature is the flexural energy, and that the first-derivative norm is the axial energy, so that the two are the complementary halves of one elastic energy rather than independent quantities. We then propose selecting the tension parameter by the bending-energy fraction φ(σ) = E bend /(E bend + Etens), a dimensionless quantity that runs monotonically from one (cubic) to zero (linear). The neutral choice φ(σ ⋆) = 1 2 corresponds to equipartition of elastic energy; the target φ ⋆ provides a single, transparent dial through which a desk may express its trade-off between smoothness and locality. The criterion is invariant under rescaling of the rate and time axes, removing the unit dependence of earlier energybased schemes. On the U.S. Treasury par-yield curve of 22-May-2026 the criterion yields a unique optimum (σ ⋆ = 4.86 at equipartition) and, relative to the natural cubic spline, reduces the hedgelocality radius of the benchmark 5-year node from 6.7 years to 0.8 year-a factor of eight-while suppressing the spurious long-end forward hump that the cubic manufactures from a flat 20-30-year segment. Across 1,064 weekly U.S. Treasury curves spanning 2006-2026, the selected tension tracks the rate regime smoothly without jumps, and the predicted inverse relationship between tension and hedge-locality radius holds out of sample with a log-correlation of-0.99.

title: Let's Talk Business: Adopting a Business Court in Louisiana

detail.title: Let's Talk Business: Adopting a Business Court in Louisiana
detail.abstract: Part I of this Comment will examine both the expansion and retrenchment of the Delaware Court of Chancery as the nation’s first specialized business court. Additionally, it will provide a brief history of the modern business courts in the United States. Part II will examine the principal justifications states have advanced for the establishment of modern business courts. Part III will propose the creation of a state business court pilot program in Louisiana, grounded in the conventional reasons for a business court with other states. It then sets forth a structured framework of recommended steps to guide implementation within Louisiana’s existing judicial system, informed by the special needs of the state and by the demonstrated best practices of business courts in other states.

title: Administrative Integration and Anti-Corruption Enforcement: Evidence from Indonesia
affiliations: Cahaya Rancamaya Boarding School

detail.title: Administrative Integration and Anti-Corruption Enforcement: Evidence from Indonesia

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Indonesia's anti-corruption apparatus is frequently read as a single story of decline, anchored to the 2019 revision of the law governing the Komisi Pemberantasan Korupsi (KPK). This paper rejects that framing as analytically thin. We treat the system instead as a configuration of incentives, monitoring relationships, and enforcement transaction costs whose outputs can be specified and evaluated. Three statutory mechanics introduced by Law No. 19/2019 form the analytical core: the relocation of the KPK into the executive cluster of state power (Article 1 angka 3 and Article 3), the interposition of a Supervisory Board (Dewan Pengawas) between investigators and their technical instruments (Articles 37A-37G), and the conversion of all KPK personnel into state civil servants (Article 1 angka 6 and Article 24(2)). We argue that these provisions did not merely weaken one agency; they restructured the principal-agent relationship at the apex of the enforcement field, producing what we term agent-capture via administrative integration a configuration in which the actors a monitoring body exists to constrain acquire leverage over that body's composition and operating conditions through ordinary personnel and supervisory law rather than through overt interference.
The analysis proceeds on three theoretical registers. Principal–Agent Theory specifies the vertical slack between the citizenry, the legislature, and the enforcement bodies, complicated in the Indonesian case by a principal — the legislature — with direct material exposure to the agent’s output. Transaction Cost Economics frames the horizontal friction among the KPK, the Indonesian National Police (Polri), and the Attorney General’s Office (Kejaksaan Agung), where overlapping mandates generate informational withholding, case-handoff delay, and forum-selection opportunities. Rent-seeking models account for the territorial dispersion of extraction under regional autonomy (Otonomi Daerah). We further assess whether Constitutional Court Decision No. 70/PUU-XVII/2019 — which converted the Supervisory Board’s ex ante authorization over wiretapping, search, and seizure into an ex post notification regime — materially restored investigative capacity or merely adjusted the procedural surface while leaving the structural changes intact. Drawing on verified enforcement data, we document a compositional reallocation of enforcement effort: the ratio of high-tier to low-tier defendants (h/ℓ) contracted by approximately 78 per cent across the preand post-amendment windows, concentrated on the central political principals who control the commission’s administrative environment, while total enforcement volume and real appropriations did not decline. The paper contends that Indonesia’s enforcement deficit is not primarily a shortfall of legal authority but a problem of misaligned incentives, redundant jurisdiction, and information asymmetry that decentralization has compounded, and it closes by specifying reform alternatives oriented toward incentive realignment rather than further statutory layering.

detail.abstract: Studies of international business, international economics and international management are particularly weak on identifying and assessing complex constellations of internationalization motives. Answers to a key question of International Business studies-why companies internationalize-contain considerable flaws. There are theoretical, disciplinary and methodological reasons for this state-of-affairs. In practice, the lacking attention for motivational constellations has serious repercussions for the theoretical sophistication of International Business (IB) studies, lowering its managerial relevance. Managers are confronted with many internationalization considerations at the same time and therefore have often difficulty in recognizing themselves in extant approaches. The abstractions that many textbooks and academic papers present on the why question of corporate internationalization, defies reality in case the various motivational trade-offs that managers face are not adequately addressed. This contribution presents a framework that is based on the identification of a number of motivational tensions that define the outcome of the actual internationalization strategies of companies: between intrinsic and extrinsic motives, strategic intent and realization, and between tactical and strategic considerations. Dealing with these tensions at the same time provides a strong ground for explaining particular outcomes of the internationalization process in degrees of international coordination and integration.

title: Diagnosing Governance Friction: Systemic Coherence in the Australian Privacy Regime

detail.title: Diagnosing Governance Friction: Systemic Coherence in the Australian Privacy Regime

The author reviewed, revised and verified all AI‑assisted content and accepts full responsibility for the final text.

detail.abstract: Governance systems rarely fail suddenly; they drift through gradual misalignments that erode coherence, legitimacy, and performance across institutional domains. This article introduces Governance Friction Analysis (GFA) as a diagnostic framework for identifying and addressing these latent strains within complex adaptive governance systems. Friction is defined as the tension or inconsistency that arises when legal, organisational, and normative systems lose alignment across interacting domains. Building on institutional design theory, complexity science, and meta-governance, GFA repositions friction as both a signal of vulnerability and a potential driver of adaptation. The method integrates qualitative coding and network mapping to locate, classify, and prioritise governance frictions across systems, and can be extended with simplified Lotka-Volterra modelling to explore dynamic trajectories of governance friction. Applying GFA to Australia's privacy governance regime reveals how structural misfits between law and technology, normative divergence between commercial and rights-based logics, and resource asymmetries in enforcement generate systemic instability. By mapping these inter-domain relationships, GFA enables early detection of governance drift and supports reform sequencing that preserves legitimacy while enhancing adaptive capacity. The framework advances public law scholarship by operationalising relational coherence as a diagnostic category and offering a replicable tool for systemic governance analysis, bridging the gap between doctrinal legality and the dynamics of legitimacy in complex, multi-level governance environments.

title: Quantum Sensors: The Underestimated Quantum Technology Strategic Implications for Civil and Defence Applications

detail.title: Quantum Sensors: The Underestimated Quantum Technology Strategic Implications for Civil and Defence Applications
detail.abstract:
Quantum sensing is the quietest of the three second-generation quantum technologies. It attracts less private capital than quantum computing, fewer international patent families, and fewer headlines. That quiet is mistaken for insignificance. It should not be.

Quantum sensors are the quantum technology closest to operational deployment. Several modalities are already shipping as commercial products. Several more will transition from prototype to field within 24 to 36 months. The military trials underway in the United Kingdom, the United States, China, and Australia are not laboratory exercises; they are operational evaluations run by flag officers to assess warfighting utility.

The global quantum sensing market was worth approximately €320 million in 2024. It is projected to reach approximately €600 million to €850 million by 2030 and approximately €1.6 to €1.9 billion by 2045. Those numbers understate the strategic reality. Quantum sensors will reshape the competitive dynamics of navigation, detection and subsurface surveillance, domains where defence doctrine, commercial aerospace, medical imaging and autonomous mobility all intersect.

This analysis advances four propositions.

First, the physics is largely done; the engineering is not. 

Second, the readiness landscape is genuinely differentiated. 

Third, quantum sensing is intrinsically dual-use.

Fourth, and this is the message European boardrooms and ministries have yet to fully absorb, Europe is not currently organised to win. 

This report is, therefore, a wake-up call. For European industrial and defence executives, the imperative is not further study. It is engagement, at scale, with conviction, and within a 24-month strategic horizon.

title: From Battlefield to Boardroom: Strategic Red Teaming as an Epistemic Governance Instrument in the Age of AI

detail.title: From Battlefield to Boardroom: Strategic Red Teaming as an Epistemic Governance Instrument in the Age of AI

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder of Apparens, a strategic advisory practice specialising in adversarial review of AI strategies. The methodology described in this paper forms the basis of Apparens' commercial service offering. No external parties influenced the research design, analysis, or conclusions.

detail.abstract:
Strategic planning in contemporary organizations proceeds, almost universally, on the assumption that the approval of a strategic initiative represents a sufficient test of its merit. It does not. The strategy approval process is characterized by advocacy rather than adversarial inquiry, and the assumptions that hold a strategy together routinely go untested until contact with operational reality forces correction at high cost. This essay argues that red teaming, an adversarial methodology originating in military doctrine and subsequently institutionalized in cybersecurity and AI safety, constitutes a structural institutional response to bounded rationality under conditions of organizational complexity, and that its application to strategy itself, rather than only to technical systems, represents not merely an extension of the methodology but a redefinition of what epistemic accountability requires at board level. 
The central research question is: under what conditions does AI integration into core organizational workflows transform strategic red teaming from a useful governance instrument into a structural fiduciary necessity? The thesis advanced is that the five structural properties of AI systems-operational leverage, transparency reduction, dependency concentration, regulatory liability, and accountability boundary shift-collectively invalidate the assumptions on which traditional risk governance rests, and that the appropriate institutional response is the formalization of strategic assumption stress testing as an independent, board-mandated, evidencegraded governance discipline. The essay contributes a formalized six-component model for Strategic Red Teaming with explicit inputs, process design, outputs, and institutional positioning, and situates this contribution relative to adjacent traditions in pre-mortem decision science, organizational debiasing research, and financial stress testing doctrine.

title: Challenges on the access to food public facilities
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of São Paulo (USP)

detail.title: Challenges on the access to food public facilities
detail.abstract: Public food and nutrition security facilities are essential for ensuring the right to adequate food and combatting hunger in cities. However, systematic analyses of the equity of their spatial distribution are rare, and existing assessments tend to rely on proximity measures that overlook the interaction between service capacity, territorial demand and urban mobility conditions. This article addresses this gap by applying an optimisation-based accessibility metric that allocates the service capacity of each facility to the population registered as requiring social protection, subject to maximum travel time constraints defined by service frequency and mode of transport. Travel-time matrices were calculated using road network, topography and public transportation data, taking actual operating hours into account. Supply was estimated using administrative data and demand was distributed across a regular hexagonal grid. The model was applied to two programmes representing distinct accessibility regimes: a subsidised meal programme operating at neighbourhood scale with daily frequency and pedestrian access, and a subsidised food market operating at city scale with lower frequency and public transit-based access. The results reveal a significant deficit: coverage rates remain below 1.2% of the estimated demand, with the installed capacity operating at full saturation. Although one program's spatial reach could theoretically cover up to 46% of demand, capacity is underallocated, showing that travel-time measures alone substantially overestimate effective access. These findings highlight the importance of combining redistributive location criteria with increased installed capacity in food security planning for large urban centres.

title: Populism and Fertility: Evidence from Developed Countries
affiliations: University of North Bengal and O. P. Jindal Global University

detail.title: Populism and Fertility: Evidence from Developed Countries
detail.abstract: The recent rise of populist governments in developed countries has generated extensive debate on their economic and institutional consequences, yet their demographic implications remain largely unexplored. This study aims to fill this research gap by highlighting that populist forms of government function in a way that extends their effects beyond the macroeconomy and quality of institutions and influences fertility decisions as well. We select countries characterised by a 'very high' level of human development where populist governments assumed power in the twenty-first century to examine the effect of populism on fertility rates. Using a quasi-natural experimental design with non-absorbing treatment, we construct a counterfactual scenario. Our findings reveal that populism increased fertility rates in these countries relative to the counterfactual control units. Thus, this study makes a significant contribution by demonstrating that fertility remains politically responsive even at advanced stages of development, offering a political-economy explanation for recent fertility pattern in the developed world.

title: Uniformly Conservative Exploration in Reinforcement Learning
affiliations: Arizona State University (ASU) - W.P. Carey School of Business, Stanford University, University of Pennsylvania - The Wharton School and University of Pennsylvania

detail.title: Uniformly Conservative Exploration in Reinforcement Learning
detail.abstract: Reinforcement learning is a promising approach for sequential decision-making problems, with applications ranging from inventory control to dynamic treatment regimes in healthcare. State-of-the-art algorithms balance exploration-exploitation tradeoff to achieve strong performance. However, in practice, unconstrained exploration can be costly or unethical, since exploratory actions may produce significantly unfavorable outcomes relative to known actions from historical data---especially when excessive exploration is concentrated within individual episodes, such as a single patient. Thus, a key challenge in deploying these algorithms is to avoid excessive exploration in individual episode and promote certain conservatism during exploration. We propose a new notion of uniformly conservative exploration, which requires the algorithm to outperform a conservative benchmark policy at every step of every episode up to a small exploration budget. The benchmark policy is not fixed a priori but is adaptively learned from all available data thus far using pessimistic value estimation. Then, we develop a novel online reinforcement learning algorithm that leverages optimistic exploration when feasible and overrides it with the conservative benchmark as needed to satisfy the exploration constraint. A key ingredient of our algorithm is the construction of meta-episodes, which stitch together adaptively determined exploration segments across multiple episodes to ensure unbiased and sufficient exploration of the entire state space. We prove that our algorithm satisfies the uniformly conservative exploration constraint with high probability. Furthermore, it achieves regret bounds that match the minimax-optimal rate for finite-horizon Markov decision processes, up to an additive term that is independent of the number of episodes and captures the cost of enforcing uniform conservatism. Finally, we evaluate our approach on inventory control and healthcare applications, demonstrating learning efficiency comparable to standard reinforcement learning methods while substantially reducing violations of the conservative exploration constraint.

title: GBC for Bayesian Model Averaging: Applications in Finance and Economics
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business and George Mason University

detail.title: GBC for Bayesian Model Averaging: Applications in Finance and Economics
detail.abstract: Bayesian model selection is a special case of parameter estimation: the model index is a latent variable, and a posterior over models is a posterior over a large discrete space. We exploit this computationally. Posterior model probabilities are computed from a vertical quantile representation-the distribution of the evidence ordinate-which generative Bayesian computation (GBC) learns by simulation and nested sampling integrates, both decoupling the cost from the 2 p enumeration of classical Bayesian model averaging (BMA). The evidence is a discrete partition function, linking the computation to the nested-sampling treatment of Potts models (Murray et al., 2006a), while the proximal L 0 algorithm of Polson and Sun (2019) returns its posterior mode at the speed of optimization. A duality (Proposition 1) identifies the model-averaged mean and the L 0 mode as two readings of one posterior, with the inclusion odds of the model prior equal to the L 0 penalty. Since the prior carries the identifying information (Steel, 2020), we catalog the structured priors of applied economics-the g-prior, its mixtures, global-local shrinkage, and the Minnesota prior of Litterman (1986)-as regularizers with explicit penalty duals. Three applications follow. In instrumental-variable regression, joint instrument/covariate selection meets the flat-likelihood pathology of Sims (2007) and Kleibergen and van Dijk (1998); our SBR-IV algorithm carries a reliability flag that, on the Card (1995) data, separates a strong instrument set (return ≈ 11%) from a weak one. In equity-premium prediction (Welch and Goyal, 2008), selection and averaging cut the kitchen-sink out-of-sample loss by 40-54 points of R 2 ; in inflation forecasting, informative predictors reverse the ordering. Moving from point to density forecasts, we reproduce the dynamic prediction pools of Del Negro et al. (2016): linear pools of Bayesian predictive densities beat Bayesian model averaging by roughly 18 log points-because averaging densities dominates averaging models when no single model is reliably best-and the pool's weight tracks financial distress. SBR is one to two orders of magnitude faster than spike-and-slab MC 3 , and GBC matches its inclusion probabilities at a 28× amortized speedup.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether and how in-person communication influences the quality of information available to market participants. We utilize the lockdown periods during the Covid-19 pandemic as a proxy for an exogenous reduction in in-person communication, and analyst forecast accuracy as a proxy for information quality. We document that when firms' headquarter states undergo lockdowns, analyst forecasts for these firms issued in the lockdown periods are significantly less accurate than for other firms or other periods, with an average difference of about 8% of the mean value of absolute forecast errors. The difference is also greater when analysts have less firm-specific experience or cover more industries, or when firms are smaller or younger. Supplemental analyses show greater differences when companies convert from in-person to virtual events despite holding more of the latter. In addition, analysts input more effort and display more divergent opinions during the lockdown periods. The collective results indicate that when there is less in-person communication, forecast quality is lower despite more effort and similar or higher frequency of virtual communication.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the long-run dynamics of real house prices in Greece and their structural drivers. We develop a Bayesian VAR model with time-varying unconditional means that allows to decompose real house prices into a slow-moving structural trend and a transitory cyclical component. The proposed empirical framework accounts for structural changes in the housing market and episodes of heightened macroeconomic volatility. Applied to Greece over 2002-2025, it identifies a pronounced and persistent upward shift in the long run house price trend from 2017 onward. Historical decomposition of the structural shocks attributes this shift mainly to self-reinforcing house price dynamics, but also to the joint effect of strong demand and constrained supply in the housing market. Allowing for time variation in the long run equilibrium of house prices yields a more appropriate assessment of potential housing market imbalances compared with a constant steady state benchmark.

detail.abstract: Climate change is intensifying riverine flood risk, yet rigorous evidence on the economic returns to large-scale inland adaptation investments remains limited. This paper provides the first national-scale causal evaluation of the Dutch Room for the River program, Europe's largest integrated inland flood-risk adaptation initiative, using more than 370,000 repeat-sale housing transactions. The program combines grey and nature-based inland flood-risk projects and is characterized by long, staggered implementation horizons. Leveraging a staggered implementation structure and a stacked difference-indifferences framework, we isolate dynamic capitalization effects at project announcement, construction, and completion. We show that project announcements increase nearby house prices by 1.9%, construction generates short-lived price declines of 2.7%, and project completion raises prices by 2.3%, with gains accumulating up to 15% over four years. Grey measures produce broader but moderate premiums, whereas nature-based solutions yield highly localized amenity-driven gains. Heterogeneity analyses reveal that capitalization is strongest in high flood-risk areas, urban neighbourhoods, and among older housing stock, consistent with both risk-reduction and amenity channels. We estimate aggregate housing wealth gains of A C 4-8 billion and benefit-cost ratios between 1.1 and 2.3. Our findings demonstrate that integrated flood-risk adaptation delivers substantial welfare benefits and highlight the complementary roles of grey and nature-based measures in climate-resilient spatial planning.

title: CBDC Pilot and Banks' Non-Performing Loans: Evidence from China

detail.title: CBDC Pilot and Banks' Non-Performing Loans: Evidence from China
detail.abstract: This study investigates the impact of China's e-CNY pilot on the nonperforming loans (NPLs) of Chinese banks. The findings show that the e-CNY pilot is associated with a significant reduction in NPLs. The effect is observed across banks of all sizes, with larger banks experiencing the strongest improvement in asset quality. When analyzed by bank type, the e-CNY pilot significantly lowers NPLs for joint-stock commercial banks, urban commercial banks, rural commercial banks, foreign-funded banks, and rural credit cooperatives, with the greatest impact seen among rural commercial banks. Conversely, NPLs of policy banks, large state-owned banks, and new rural financial institutions show no significant change. These findings suggest that the introduction of a central bank digital currency can enhance banks' credit quality while posing no adverse effects on loan performance, providing valuable guidance for policymakers considering CBDC implementation.

title: FinPersona: A Multi-Layered Framework for Personality-Aware Financial Copilots Integrating Trust Calibration, Financial Literacy, and Shared Autonomy

detail.title: FinPersona: A Multi-Layered Framework for Personality-Aware Financial Copilots Integrating Trust Calibration, Financial Literacy, and Shared Autonomy
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is moving from the operational periphery of financial services toward the point of consumer contact, and finance-tuned large language models are giving rise to conversational "copilots" intended to advise, educate, and in some configurations act on users' behalf. This paper argues that current consumer-facing financial AI systems remain insufficient in interrelated ways: personalisation is shallow, trust calibration is treated as an afterthought rather than a design objective, digital financial literacy is cultivated apart from advisory interaction, the allocation of control between user and system is undertheorised in finance, and governance is frequently asserted rather than mechanised. The deeper problem is that the research streams most relevant to such systems-finance-tuned model capability, trust in automation, digital financial literacy, and shared autonomy have developed in isolation, leaving no integrative account of how these concerns should be jointly configured. The paper develops FinPersona, a six-layer conceptual framework for personality-aware financial copilots that integrates user modelling, adaptive agent personas, recommendation generation and communication, trust calibration, shared autonomy, and governance into a single architecture in which each layer constrains the others. The framework makes three conservatively stated contributions: an integrative specification of how the constructs relate; a diagnostic and normative principle subordinating agent persona to trust calibration in response to the documented misalignment between persona-driven trust and advice quality; and a programmatic set of testable propositions sorted by evidentiary tier. FinPersona is presented as a conceptual architecture and a research agenda, not as a validated or implemented system; its claims are calibrated to the strength of available evidence, and components resting on weaker grounding notably the personality axis and the transfer of shared-autonomy logic from robotics are identified as requiring prior validation. The framework's implications for designers, institutions, regulators, and educators are framed as conditional design guidance.

detail.abstract:
This paper examines the evolution of Japanese capital outflows from 1950 to 2025 through the combined lenses of macroeconomic and microeconomic theoretical approches . While the literature often analyzes capital exports through either national savings, exchange rates, monetary policy, and demographic change, or through firm-level decisions regarding foreign direct investment, this study argues that both perspectives are necessary to understand the long-run transformation of Japanese capital flows.

Drawing on historical evidence and international macroeconomic data, the paper analyzes the transition of Japan from a post-war industrial economy to the world's largest net creditor nation. It highlights the role of high domestic savings, financial liberalization, exchange rate dynamics following the Plaza Accord, prolonged low interest rates, demographic ageing, and the internationalization strategies of Japanese firms. Particular attention is given to the changing composition of external surpluses, which progressively shifted from trade-based surpluses toward investment income generated abroad.

The findings suggest that Japanese capital outflows cannot be adequately explained by macroeconomic or microeconomic factors alone. Rather, their evolution reflects the interaction between national economic conditions and firm-level strategic responses to changes in costs, demand, demographics, and global financial conditions. The Japanese experience provides broader insights into the determinants of international capital movements in advanced economies facing demographic ageing and financial globalization.

title: The Professional Bundle: Execution, Judgment, and Accountability in an Age of AI

detail.title: The Professional Bundle: Execution, Judgment, and Accountability in an Age of AI
detail.abstract:
Professions are not organized around expertise. They are organized around accountability. Accountability is not an end in itself, but instead the institutional architecture that makes professional trust rational: the mechanism through which relying on someone whose work you cannot evaluate becomes something other than a wager. The license, the fiduciary obligation, and the malpractice framework do not exist to constrain expertise; they exist to make trust possible.

This paper argues that licensed professions have historically bundled three functions within a single role: execution, judgment, and accountability. The bundle persisted because its components were economically interdependent. Artificial intelligence alters that equilibrium by compressing the cost of execution asymmetrically. Unlike prior productivity tools, which improved execution while preserving the relative economics of the bundle, AI reduces the marginal cost of significant categories of professional execution while leaving the value of judgment and accountability largely intact. By changing their relative economics, it creates the conditions under which the bundled functions become economically separable. This paper calls this professional decomposition.

The decomposition follows a predictable sequence. Execution decomposes first because it is most mechanically describable. Judgment decomposes unevenly: pattern recognition and information synthesis are highly automatable, while variable selection, value prioritization, and responsibility acceptance are structurally resistant. Accountability decomposes last and most reluctantly because it is constitutive of professional status rather than incidental to it. This paper develops a taxonomy of judgment components and their AI trajectories and identifies two failure modes—cognitive surrender and cognitive rust—through which the accountability function can be hollowed out from within even as formal professional structures remain intact.

Drawing on the Kirkland & Ellis AI platform announcement of June 2026, ABA Formal Opinion 512, Federal Reserve SR 26-2, and this author’s direct professional experience across legal, medical, and accounting accountability structures, this paper develops three scenarios for how accountability evolves as the bundle comes apart: remaining professional, becoming institutional, or becoming distributed. It argues that institutional accountability is an acceptable evolved form of the professional bargain, but only if the governance architecture that makes it credible is deliberately built. The profession has a window to design that architecture before litigation and regulation design it by default. The window is not open indefinitely.

title: Passive Flows, Active Woes: Passive Investing and the Decline of Active Mutual Fund Alpha

detail.title: Passive Flows, Active Woes: Passive Investing and the Decline of Active Mutual Fund Alpha
detail.abstract: This paper studies whether the secular shift toward passive investing has affected active fund performance through flow-induced demand effects. Using U.S. equity fund data (1984-2024), I document a decline in active fund performance after 2010, with average annual four-factor alpha falling by around one percentage point and the previously positive relation between Active Share and performance reversing. These patterns contrast with theories predicting improved performance as the active sector shrinks. A flow-driven framework shows that capital reallocations toward passive funds generate asymmetric price pressure, penalizing funds' active tilts. Flow-induced demand significantly impacts fund returns, with the effects of passive flows persisting over multiple years. Controlling for flow-induced trading can explain the negative Active Share-performance relationship, suggesting that underperformance reflects structural demand headwinds rather than declining manager skill. Higher-frequency tests exploiting plausibly exogenous, beginning-of-month passive flows provide additional evidence.

detail.title: Hardware-Aware Multi-Objective Neural Architecture Search via NSGA-II and Random Search for Li-ion Battery SOC Estimation under Microcontroller-Class Constraints
detail.abstract: Deploying deep learning for state-of-charge (SOC) estimation on resource-constrained battery management systems (BMS) is critical for platforms under stringent Size, Weight, and Power (SWaP) constraints, yet existing data-driven approaches optimize accuracy alone and address model complexity and latency only after architecture selection, so the resulting designs often fail to meet edge deployment budgets. We propose a multi-objective neural architecture search (NAS) framework that integrates NSGA-II and Random Search via a Combined Pareto Front, evaluating CNN, LSTM, GRU, and Transformer families in a unified search space at an identical 300-trial budget per algorithm. Pareto-optimal candidates pass through a three-dimensional Edge-Realistic Ideal Zone grounded in deployment envelopes: Val MAE < 0.025 (±5% SOC band per automotive BMS practice), FLOPs < 2.0 M (ARM Cortex-M7 real-time throughput), and parameter count < 30 K (ARM Cortex-M3 SRAM). On the NASA (long-term degradation) and CALCE (dynamic stress test) datasets with five-run repeated training, the preferred architecture depends on analysis depth: NASA's Ideal Zone admits exclusively GRU candidates (5/5) while CALCE admits a mixed CNN/GRU/LSTM composition, yet once five-run robustness validation is applied, both converge to GRU as the sole val_safe main candidate — Trial 208 for NASA (16,161 params, 1.49 MFLOPs, val MAE 0.0119 ± 0.0015) and Trial 136 for CALCE (2,737 params, 0.058 MFLOPs, val MAE 0.0180 ± 0.0016). NSGA-II accounts for 80% of Ideal Zone candidates across both datasets and 100% on CALCE, concentrating trials where deployment constraints bind. By embedding hardware constraints directly in the search loop, the framework supports SOC estimation across SWaP-constrained platforms — unmanned vehicles, electric vehicles, and stationary energy storage.

title: The Relational Fallout of Addiction: A Phenomenological Study of Wives Navigating a Partner's Substance Use Disorder
affiliations: University of Kashmir and Dept of Social Work, University of Kashmir

detail.title: The Relational Fallout of Addiction: A Phenomenological Study of Wives Navigating a Partner's Substance Use Disorder
detail.abstract: Substance Use Disorder (SUD) represents a critical global public health crisis, exacting a devastating toll on individual health, familial stability, and communal cohesion. Its repercussions ripple outward, ensnaring family members in a complex web of psychological distress, social stigma, and practical hardship. While the impact of SUD is pervasive, its manifestation is profoundly personal and often gendered, varying significantly across different familial roles. This paper explores the lived experiences of wives whose husbands have a Substance Use Disorder (SUD). The aim is to understand the profound personal and social challenges these women face, highlighting the urgent need for better support systems.Using a qualitative approach, Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA), the study delves into the subjective experiences of ten wives from Jammu and Kashmir, India. Participants, aged 22-39 and from varied literacy and economic backgrounds, were recruited from a drug de-addiction centre. In-depth interviews lasting 60-90 minutes were conducted, transcribed, and analysed thematically.The findings reveal six core themes of suffering: Broken Trust and Betrayal, where women discovered the addiction after marriage, often with family complicity; Financial Instability and Future Uncertainty, leading to poverty and constant anxiety; Family and Marital Conflict, involving blame from in-laws and eroded relationships; Children’s Compromised Futures, with mothers taking extreme steps to shield their children; Intimate Partner Violence, a normalized outcome of addiction cycles; and the Dilemma of Divorce, where women feel trapped by stigma, economic dependence, and family honour.In conclusion, a husband’s SUD creates a catastrophic, multi-layered crisis for his spouse, extending far beyond the individual addict. The study calls for a shift towards non-judgmental, family-centered care, economic support, and community-level reforms to address this systemic entrapment and support the women bearing its heaviest burden.

detail.title: Breeding for resistance and defence responses to root lesion-forming nematodes in Banana: Insights from biochemical and metabolomics analysis to histological differences between resistant and susceptible genotypes
detail.abstract: Root lesion-forming nematodes (RLFN), the most damaging pest in banana, cause severe root necrosis, reduced nutrient uptake, plant toppling, and yield loss. Hence, host-plant resistance offers the best alternative. This study aimed to develop banana hybrids using diverse diploid, triploid, and tetraploid parents and to identify high-yielding, resistant hybrids. A total of 8359 crosses were made, and 49 hybrids were established and screened against RLFN under field and pot experiments. The findings revealed substantial variability in bunch weight (BW) and associated traits and identified 18 resistant and 17 tolerant hybrids under field conditions. Furthermore, the hybrids H-11-18, H-11-21, H-11-23, H-11-25, H-11-44, H-11-69 and H-11-71 with BW>10kg were validated for their resistance to Radopholus similis in a pot experiment and were found resistant except for one tolerant hybrid (H-11-18). Crosses involving at least one resistant parent produced the highest proportion of resistant progenies, underscoring the importance of resistant parental lines. Additionally, the biochemical study revealed elevated phenol and lignin content in resistant genotypes upon nematode infection, indicating a key defence mechanism. In support of this, histochemical analysis of roots revealed intense and predominant localisation of phenol and lignin in resistant genotypes. Correspondingly, the histological study showed more compact and continuous cellular organization in Yangambi Km5, forming an effective barrier to nematode penetration. Importantly, GC-MS revealed a diverse metabolite profile in resistant genotypes. In conclusion, the findings led to the development of high-yielding, resistant hybrids and to a deeper understanding of nematode-plant interactions.

detail.abstract: IT governance frameworks derived from commercial enterprise research, principally Sambamurthy and Zmud's (1999) contingency theory and Weill and Ross's (2004) specification of IT decision rights and accountability structures, carry an implicit scope condition the literature has not made explicit: their contingency variables omit organizational mission type, and their assumptions about IT value delivery do not hold for organizations whose primary output is knowledge creation rather than knowledge application. This article identifies that scope condition and demonstrates, through a convergent synthesis across transaction cost economics, the organizational theory of knowledge-intensive organizations, public administration empirics, and organizational enabling conditions theory, that research-intensive public organizations (federal research agencies, federally funded research and development centers, national laboratories, and academic health centers) require a different IT governance logic. I introduce the Mission-Stratified IT Governance framework, a three-tier governance architecture that differentiates IT work by asset specificity and mission coupling. Commodity IT is governed through enterprise centralization, where existing frameworks apply within their validated scope; context-aware research-enabling services through federated coordination on open standards, designed as enabling rather than coercive formalization (Adler & Borys, 1996); and missionspecific research IT as a dynamic capability whose governance preserves the institutional knowledge proximity on which its value depends. Five diagnostic tests determine tier assignment, and an explicit reassessment mechanism addresses governance tier migration as technologies and research programs evolve. The framework makes three theoretical contributions: it identifies organizational mission type as a structural gap in the contingency variable sets of existing IT governance frameworks; it specifies a theorized governance tier for research-enabling services not present in prior IT governance work; and it offers a diagnostic apparatus for centralization decisions in organizations where governance error carries direct costs to scientific productivity. The contribution is a boundary-condition identification and theory extension: existing frameworks retain their validity within their scope, and the Mission-Stratified framework specifies the architecture appropriate to the organizational class that falls outside it.

detail.abstract: A structural shift. Google AI Overviews are changing how citizens access public-interest information online. Users increasingly receive synthesised answers within Google's own interface without visiting publisher websites, shifting attention and commercial value away from the original source and towards the platform. Traffic and revenue effects. The available evidence points in a consistent direction: AI-generated summaries reduce visits to publishers' websites. Behavioural research documents a sharp drop in clickthrough rates whenever an AI Overview appears, a pattern that industry studies consistently corroborate. Media leaders also expect a substantial further decline in search referral traffic over the coming years. European evidence remains thinner because rollout came later, but similar pressures are likely to emerge, with smaller, regional and minority-language publishers especially exposed. A democratic-resilience problem. The issue has a structural dimension that copyright and revenue disputes alone cannot capture. AI-generated summaries may reduce the visibility of competing editorial framings and reinforce existing hierarchies of source visibility, making this, at its core, a media-pluralism and democratic-resilience problem.

detail.title: A Path to Lasting Peace: Proposal for a Neutral Guarantor to Facilitate Israeli-Palestinian Relations

detail.abstract:
This paper proposes a Neutral Guarantor Framework as an alternative diplomatic mechanism for facilitating Israeli–Palestinian relations under international law. Drawing upon Chapter VI of the Charter of the United Nations,1 the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations (1961),2 and historical precedents involving protecting powers and neutral mediation states, the paper introduces a legally grounded framework through which a neutral state or multilateral guarantor council may support diplomatic engagement, crisis communication, conflict deescalation, and implementation oversight. 

The study evaluates the structural weaknesses that contributed to the failure of major peace initiatives between 1947 and 2020, including the Oslo Accords,3 the Camp David negotiations,4 the Road Map for Peace,5 and subsequent bilateral diplomatic frameworks. It argues that the absence of a trusted and permanent neutral intermediary, combined with diplomatic asymmetry and inconsistent enforcement mechanisms, significantly undermined sustainable conflict resolution efforts. 

The proposed framework seeks neither to replace sovereignty nor to impose external governance. Rather, it aims to establish a structured diplomatic channel capable of promoting accountability, continuity, and mutual confidence while preserving the sovereign integrity of both Israelis and Palestinians. The paper further examines potential guarantor states according to criteria of neutrality, institutional credibility, peacebuilding experience, and international legitimacy. 

The article concludes that a Neutral Guarantor Framework represents a realistic and legally viable diplomatic innovation capable of complementing existing international peace efforts and contributing to long-term regional stability.

detail.abstract: Existing literature has established that International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Doc 9303, the Machine-Readable Travel Document (MRTD) standard upon which many countries base their passports and identity cards, mandates cryptographic algorithms foreseeably vulnerable to forgery by Cryptographically Relevant Quantum Computers (CRQCs). This paper's threefold contribution is integrated framing of MRTD quantum cryptographic exposures. First, a structured literature review at the intersection of MRTDs and Post-quantum Cryptography (PQC) shows cryptographic mechanisms being studied whilst holistic MRTD failure modes remain unframed. Second, an application of the author's Quantum Attack Surface Modelling (QASM) procedure diagnoses MRTDs as a limiting case in which organisational control is near zero, so the only reasonable response is consequence mitigation. Third, the QASM application reveals that the modern externalised border, which projects identity decisions extraterritorially, depends upon the reliability of MRTDs' identity bindings, amplifying the quantum cryptographic exposure of MRTDs. The foreseeable consequences are priority ordered: first for trusted travel, border control and lawful migration; thereafter for finance and employment identity checks. Two findings follow. Drawing on security-economics, MRTD quantum exposures persist because their costs fall on parties who neither control the cryptography nor record it in their accounts and risk registers, no risk taxonomy carrying a category for a forged trust anchor. A corollary of the MRTD limited control case is that technical PQC research fails to reach the fielded estate, so the unaddressed gap is economic and cross-sectoral rather than cryptographic.

title: Behavioral Risk Profiling across Five Countries: Loss Aversion, Risk Aversion, and the Reflection Effect
affiliations: University of Essex - Department of Economics and University of Antwerp

detail.title: Behavioral Risk Profiling across Five Countries: Loss Aversion, Risk Aversion, and the Reflection Effect
detail.abstract: Risk profiling typically reduces investors' preferences to a single risk-return trade-off, despite extensive evidence that reference dependence plays a central role in decisions under risk and uncertainty. We show that three elicited indifference values are sufficient to jointly identify loss aversion and domain-specific risk attitudes over gains and losses, thereby measuring the reflection effect as a shift toward greater risk seeking in the loss domain, without imposing functional-form assumptions. Using data from over 25,000 respondents in five European countries, we find that loss aversion and the reflection effect differ markedly in prevalence: loss aversion is far from universal, with the median respondent loss neutral in three of the five countries, whereas the reflection effect is observed for the majority of respondents in every country. We further show that widely used survey-based risk questionnaires primarily capture gain-domain risk attitudes and provide little information about loss aversion or the reflection effect. These findings imply that substantially richer behavioral profiling is feasible without increasing survey complexity. The method provides a tractable tool for researchers interested in measuring these preferences at scale and has practical applications in personalized financial services, such as investor suitability assessments.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Texas A&M University School of Law Legal Studies Research Paper

detail.abstract: While a rich body of scholarship explored how emotions influence decisions over the use and allocation of water resources, a comprehensive review that synthesizes and integrates recent advances in understanding the role emotions play in water governance and management decision-making is lacking. This study implements a systematic scoping review utilizing Boolean literature searching technique to extract emotional connotations concerning water and environmental governance in English language scholarly records in Web of Science and Scopus databases. Drawing on emotional geography of water, this systematic review explores the emotional dispositions of communities between 2000-2025 at both intra-basin and inter-basin levels through the lens of spatial, temporal, and political nexuses. We contend that communities, particularly those that are marginalized, manifest deep emotional attachments to the flow of shared water at the temporal, political and spatial scales. These under-served communities, which are denied historical access to water (temporal nexus) and whose sacred spaces and landscapes (spatial nexus) are often occupied under colonialism (political nexus), experience deeply collective emotional distress resulting in the loss of their identity. Although this research lays the foundation for exploration of the emotional geography of water through an integrated, spatialized, temporalized and politicized landscape, we contend that a number of interrelated , but important factors have been unexplored. This study suggests that examining the emotional dynamics of under-served communities, particularly Indigenous communities, through diverse cultural and linguistic perspectives will further enlighten the discourse of the emotional geography of water. Indeed, these narratives unravel how different communities feel, experience, value and connect to water. Such a nuanced view will lead to a more inclusive and comprehensive understanding of the emotional geography of water.

detail.title:
Superposition as Geometry: 
Grassmann Manifold Structure of Neural Representations
detail.abstract: Neural superposition-the phenomenon by which networks represent more features than they have neurons-is typically described as a statistical or informationtheoretic phenomenon. We show it is fundamentally geometric. A weight matrix W (n × m) defines a single point V = row(W) ∈ Gr(n, m) on the Grassmann manifold, and the superposition loss is the expected squared projection error onto V ⊥ : L super = E[∥P V ⊥ x∥ 2 ] (Theorem 3.1). All known thresholds-packing (k < n), spark recovery (k < n/2), Donoho-Tanner, CDMA spectral efficiency-are instances of a single question: for what load λ = k/n does the projection π : Σ k → V cease to be injective? From this perspective we derive three new results. First, we prove the Gini coefficient G(α) of the feature-frequency distribution measures anisotropy of the feature-usage measure on Σ k (Theorem 5.2), providing a quantitative bridge between the uniform-importance model and real networks. Second, we derive the SAE width scaling law m SAE < n/(2ᾱ) as a direct corollary of the injectivity condition (Corollary 6.1). Third, we track the trajectory V 0 ,. .. , V 11 of GPT-2 small representation subspaces on Gr(768, 100), finding a 1.33× larger Grassmann step at the embedding-to-contextual transition and near-constant steps thereafter, with middle layers collapsing to near-degenerate r 95 = 1-6 dimensional subspaces.

detail.title: Sustainability-Adjusted Credit Guarantee Pricing for Financing Micro, Small, and Medium-Sized Enterprises in Malaysia

publicationDetails.detailsText: ADB Economics Working Paper Series No. 852

detail.abstract: As in many Asian economies, Malaysia’s micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) account for the vast majority of firms and large shares of economic output and employment. Their significant carbon footprint makes them pivotal for achieving carbon neutrality. In bank-dominated financial systems such as Malaysia’s, credit guarantees help facilitate lending to MSMEs. This paper proposes a way to both ease MSME access to finance and incentivize decarbonization and sustainability. It develops a risk-based and sustainability-adjusted credit guarantee pricing framework that integrates an MSME’s financial health, environmental footprint, and the macroeconomic conditions it faces. Using financial data from 2,000 Malaysian MSMEs, principal component analysis is used to construct a financial health index, followed by K-means clustering to classify firms by risk. A countercyclical pricing model produces a firm‑level credit guarantee fee ranging from 1.08% for the healthiest firms during a recession to 2.58% for the riskiest firms during economic expansion. Firm-level sustainability survey data are used to build a composite performance score which reduces guarantee fees by an average of 0.13 percentage points, with a reduction up to 0.23 percentage points for top-performing firms.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the implementation of Just-In-Time (JIT) methodology in the production planning of Lajvar Industrial Group, a leading Iranian manufacturer of hydraulic aerial work platforms and truckmounted cranes. The study addresses persistent operational inefficiencies including high inventory levels, extended production lead times, and interdepartmental coordination failures. Through a mixedmethods approach combining structured questionnaires, face-to-face interviews, KPI monitoring, and regression analysis across a sample of 80 production personnel, the research evaluates the quantitative impact of JIT on four key performance indicators: production time, product quality, productivity, and operational costs. Regression analysis demonstrates statistically significant improvements across all variables (p < 0.001). Production lead time was reduced by 40% (from 25 to 15 days per product cycle), defect rates halved from 8% to 4%, productivity increased by 20% (from 75 to 90 units per labour hour), and production costs decreased by approximately 28%. The implementation involved Kanban systems, U-shaped production line redesign, ERP integration, supplier evaluation frameworks, and comprehensive employee training programmes. Findings contribute to the growing literature on JIT applicability in complex, multi-product heavy manufacturing environments in emerging industrial economies, and offer a structured implementation model transferable to similar industrial contexts.

title: Momentum vs. Fundamentals: What Drives Short-Term Stock Returns in India?

detail.title: Momentum vs. Fundamentals: What Drives Short-Term Stock Returns in India?
detail.abstract: This paper poses a specific question: which of price momentum or the 52-week high signal does better to predict short-term stock returns in India and does this differ if large, mid or small-cap stocks are considered? Employing 431 stocks from all three segments (large-, mid-, and small-cap) of the Indian equity market between January 2015 to December 2023, we form tertile sorted portfolios on the intermediate momentum signal r(12,2), based on Jegadeesh and Titman (1993) with George and Hwang (2004) 52-week highs ratio, in addition to test their individual predictive power as well as joint across holding periods of one-, three-and six-month. We find that while both signals identify high-performing assets across all size segments-the results diverge significantly by size. In big-caps, all strategies deliver statistically insignificant WML spreads driven by strong loser portfolio returns. The 52-week high strategy in mid-caps generates a substantial WML of 0.987% per month, beating momentum (0.740%). For small-caps, the momentum leads at 0.903% to 0.782%, but both of these numbers are very marginally result as well. The full-universe results make it clear that extending beyond large-caps changes the landscape significantly-combined momentum WML at 0.905% (t = 2.298), and 52-week high WML of 0.726% (t = 1.874) are both nontrivial. One would think that gains would come from holding longer with either of the two strategies, yet the reversal effect for both profits decays over time but impressively enough, for midcaps the 52 week high effect is fairly stable for one three and six month horizons. After COVID, both strategies bounce back strongly in mid and small-caps and revert the large-cap 52-week high effect. This suggests that it matters a great deal where you look in the Indian market-the same anomalies appearing to be missing in the Nifty 100 are alive and well elsewhere in the broader universe.

detail.title: Tourism Shock, Labour Market Vulnerability, and Household Welfare in Cambodia: Evidence from a Social Accounting Matrix Multiplier Analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There is no conflict of interest for this study.

detail.abstract: Tourism is one of Cambodia's most important engines of growth, contributing to income, foreign exchange earnings, enterprise activity, employment, and household livelihoods. Although Cambodia's tourism sector recovered strongly after the COVID-19 crisis, recent external shock weakened tourism sector in 2025, suggesting a decline of 1.13 million international arrival, or 16.9 percent year-on-year. This study examines the economy-wide and labour market consequences of this tourism demand shock using a Social Accounting Matrix framework. The results indicate that this direct shock generates a wider economy-wide output loss of about USD 3.73 billion, equivalent to approximately 1.1 percent of baseline output. The shock affects around 110,035 jobs which is about 1.2% of the total employment, with the burden concentrated among self-employed workers, informal workers, low-skilled labour, and tourism-linked service activities. Informal jobs and self-employed jobs are affected, suggesting social sensitivity of the shock. Factor income declines across all skill groups with low-skilled labour experiencing the largest proportional loss. Household income falls across both urban and rural household groups, indicating that tourism shocks transmit through both direct service-sector employment and indirect agricultural and supply-chain linkages. The study provides evidence that tourism recovery policy in Cambodia should move beyond visitor promotion alone and integrate market diversification, employment protection, SME liquidity support, domestic tourism development, local supply-chain strengthening, and institutionalized tourism shock monitoring.

title: Trade Implications of Digital Regulation in Asia-Pacific
affiliations: and United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP)

detail.title: Trade Implications of Digital Regulation in Asia-Pacific
detail.abstract: Digital trade has been fueling global economic growth. While the significance of the regulatory environment is increasingly acknowledged, empirical evidence on its trade effects remains limited—particularly within the Asia-Pacific context. Drawing on the Asia-Pacific Regional Digital Trade Integration Index 2.0 (RDTII 2.0), developed by the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) in 2024, this study conducts a regionally grounded and domain-comprehensive analysis across 22 economies and 12 distinct policy areas. Structural gravity models are employed to estimate the effects of both domestic regulation and inter-economy regulatory convergence on trade in ICT goods and digitally deliverable services. A synthetic model integrating elastic net, random forests, and extreme gradient boosting, optimized via nested cross-validation, further uncovers the political economy dynamics underlying regulatory configurations. The results reveal that restrictive regulation significantly curtails digital trade across most policy domains, with identified domains exerting markedly stronger effects. Although regulatory convergence generally enhances trade, its effect is conditional on the domestic regulatory context, which itself appears to reflect a hybrid logic shaped by both political accountability and economic development. These findings advance the global understanding of digital trade governance through an Asia-Pacific lens, offering timely insights for researchers and policymakers seeking to align domestic reform with international cooperation in the digital era.

title: Setting the Recycled-Content Ceiling: Certifiable Supply, Chain-of-Custody Recognition, and the EV-versus-Storage scope of China's Battery mandate under the EU Battery Regulation

detail.title: Setting the Recycled-Content Ceiling: Certifiable Supply, Chain-of-Custody Recognition, and the EV-versus-Storage scope of China's Battery mandate under the EU Battery Regulation

The author has no direct financial relationships with any of the battery manufacturers, recyclers, or government agencies referenced in this paper.
