title: Dynamic Account Reference System: An Interactive Educational Tool for Introductory Financial Accounting
affiliations: Central Michigan University and Central Michigan University - College of Business Administration

detail.title: Dynamic Account Reference System: An Interactive Educational Tool for Introductory Financial Accounting

publicationDetails.detailsText: Accepted at Journal of Education for Business

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Dynamic Account Reference System (DARS), an interactive educational tool designed to enhance the learning experience for students in introductory financial accounting courses. 1 The tool provides an interactive platform where students can explore accounting accounts, understand their definitions, and view journal entry examples through a user-friendly interface. The tool features a comprehensive database of 30 common accounting accounts across all five major categories (Assets, Liabilities, Equity, Revenue, and Expenses), each with detailed definitions and transaction scenarios. The use of this tool can significantly improve student engagement and comprehension of foundational accounting concepts.

title: Technological Monopoly Rent: A Category for the Political Economy of the New Productive Forces

detail.title: Technological Monopoly Rent: A Category for the Political Economy of the New Productive Forces

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This paper does not report research involving human participants or patient data; no ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding supported this research.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a category for the political economy of the artificial-intelligence era: Technological Monopoly Rent (TMR), defined as the value extracted from controlling access to productive capacities whose underlying outputs approach zero marginal cost. The central claim is that value in the era of the new productive forces is captured not principally as profit on living labor, nor as ordinary monopoly markup in a contestable market, but as rent on enclosed productive capacity. TMR is distinguished here from classical profit, from Marxian surplus value, and from standard monopoly rent along three structural axes. Its productive base is appropriated from a collective commons rather than purchased. It is extracted in exchange with no living labor in the production of each unit. And its non-rival, near-zero-marginal-cost structure makes the competitive equilibrium of standard theory unstable, so that concentration is the market's attractor rather than its pathology. The paper then offers the operative decomposition: technological monopoly rent resolves into a compute monopoly, a model monopoly, and a permission monopoly, corresponding respectively to control of the physical training substrate, control of the trained productive capacity built on appropriated knowledge, and control of metered access to a good whose marginal cost is effectively nil. The same enclosure structure recurs across six "productive-force ruptures" (AI, quantum computation, brain-computer interfaces, gene editing, robotics, and fusion) coupled into a single reinforcing system. A readable formal statement of the rent and of its cross-domain coupling is provided. The full treatment, with the complete empirical apparatus, appears in An Invitation After Abundance (Chen 2026, ISBN 979-8-9960105-0-9).

title: State-Level Utility Regulation in Nigeria: Establishing Feed-in Tariffs for Distributed Renewable Energy
affiliations: Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta, Ogun State, Nigeria, Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta, Ogun State, Nigeria and Covenant University

detail.title: State-Level Utility Regulation in Nigeria: Establishing Feed-in Tariffs for Distributed Renewable Energy
detail.abstract: Nigeria's recent decentralization of its electricity market under the Electricity Act 2023 empowers state governments to independently regulate distributed generation (DG). However, sub-national utility commissions currently lack the localized economic benchmarks necessary to design bankable Feed-in Tariffs (FiTs). Addressing this critical regulatory gap, this study evaluates the commercial viability of 20 MW standalone solar (PSS) and wind (WSS) systems, aligning with current regulatory capacity limits, across Nigeria's six geopolitical zones. Utilizing two decades (2003-2022) of ground-measured meteorological data from the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMET), the methodology integrates a comprehensive loss-stack framework and varied debtequity structures to evaluate the Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE), Net Present Cost (NPC), and minimum FiT thresholds. These economic outputs are subsequently benchmarked against the prevailing cost-reflective Band-A tariff (₦134.08/kWh). The findings demonstrate that wind assets in high-resource corridors significantly outperform solar baselines; under a standard 50:50 debtto-equity structure, minimum FiTs for wind (WSS) range from a highly competitive $0.13/kWh in Jos to $0.35/kWh in Iseyin. Conversely, solar configurations (PSS) require higher FiTs ranging from $0.31/kWh in Maiduguri to $0.46/kWh in Port Harcourt, reflecting constrained capacity factors. These results highlight a substantial deficit between current centralized tariffs and actual private investor requirements. Ultimately, this research provides the essential, location-specific 2 pricing benchmarks needed by state regulators to de-risk decentralized renewable investments, thereby advancing Nigeria's Energy Transition Plan and SDG 7.

title: Market Access Insight Series

detail.title: Market Access Insight Series
detail.abstract: Background: Precision medicine has transformed oncology drug development and health technology assessment (HTA). Biomarker-guided therapies generate large treatment effects, compelling biological rationale, and improved cost-effectiveness profiles, creating a widespread perception that molecular specificity reduces the evidentiary burden associated with NICE decision-making. Objective This paper challenges that perception. The central argument is that precision medicine does not eliminate uncertainty; it relocates uncertainty from population heterogeneity toward alternative domains including small-sample inference, biomarker validity, assay performance, basket trial methodology, external validity, treatment sequencing, and long-term outcome estimation. This argument is developed against an explicit comparator baseline: the uncertainty profile of conventional broad-population oncology trials evaluated by NICE. Methods A conceptual framework distinguishing five operationally defined uncertainty categories-clinical, statistical, structural, external validity, and decisionis developed, mapped against a conventional oncology baseline, and applied to three NICE technology appraisals: selpercatinib for RET fusion-positive NSCLC (TA756); larotrectinib for NTRK fusion-positive solid tumours; and sotorasib for KRAS G12Cmutated NSCLC (TA830). The framework is situated within the existing HTA uncertainty taxonomy literature. Results Across all three case studies, strong biological precision and compelling efficacy signals coexisted with substantial residual uncertainty in comparative effectiveness, long-term survival, treatment sequencing, and assay standardisationdomains in which conventional broad-population trials typically offer stronger evidence. NICE issued conditional positive recommendations via the Cancer Drugs Fund in each case. A structured cross-case comparison confirms that the relocation pattern is consistent across different molecular contexts and trial architectures. Discussion Biological plausibility strengthens prior confidence in observed effects but cannot substitute for empirical evidence on comparative effectiveness, durability, or real-world generalisability. Manufacturers must plan evidence generation programmes adequate to the distinctive uncertainty profile of biomarker-defined populations. Conclusion The analytical discipline applied to population-level oncology evidence must be applied with equal rigour to biomarker-defined evidence. Increasing biological specificity does not remove the need for structured uncertainty assessment. HTA methodological development must keep pace with the evolving precision oncology paradigm.

title: What Drives Firms to Go Green? Cross-Country Evidence from Enterprise Surveys

detail.title: What Drives Firms to Go Green? Cross-Country Evidence from Enterprise Surveys
detail.abstract: This paper examines the determinants of firms' CO 2 monitoring and energy management adoption using the data from the World Bank Enterprise Surveys. Firm-level covariates, including size, sector, age and capabilities e.g. employee training, process innovation, R&D, foreign technology use, financial inclusion, and quality certification, are the strongest and most consistent predictors of environmental action. Experience with climate shocks and government procurement contracts also raises probability that firms engage in the adoption of environmentally responsible practices. At the country level, national environmental performance (EPI) increases the likelihood of green practices, while governance quality matters mainly for energy management. Newly constructed Business Ready Environmental Index does not explain much of crosscountry variation in CO 2 monitoring or energy management adoption. Overall, internal capabilities dominate in shaping firms' environmental behavior.

title: Beyond Profit Maximization: Long-Run Bankruptcy Risk, Continuous Stress, and the True Cost of Debt-Financed Growth

detail.title: Beyond Profit Maximization: Long-Run Bankruptcy Risk, Continuous Stress, and the True Cost of Debt-Financed Growth
detail.abstract: Standard theory frames the borrowing decision as a comparison between the marginal return on borrowed capital and the rate of interest: a firm should borrow whenever an extra unit of debt raises current profit. This paper argues that the comparison is incomplete. Debt does not merely expand capital; it also raises the firm's long-run exposure to insolvency and imposes a continuous, non-pecuniary burden on the people attached to the firm-owners, managers, workers, families, suppliers, and communities. We embed these two "hidden" costs in an otherwise classical model. Bankruptcy is treated as a cumulative-hazard process, so that even a small annual probability of failure compounds into a large probability over a long horizon; stress is treated as a convex flow cost that accrues every period the debt is outstanding. The borrowing problem then becomes the maximization of long-run welfare rather than current profit. The central result is a modified optimality condition in which debt is worthwhile only while its marginal operating return exceeds the marginal expected bankruptcy loss plus the marginal stress cost. Because the classical rule omits both terms, privately "optimal" leverage is systematically excessive. A numerical illustration shows the gap can be large: in our calibration the profit-maximizing firm borrows more than three times the welfare-maximizing amount, and the additional borrowing turns positive welfare into a substantial loss well before any default actually occurs. The framework reinterprets the choice between aggressive leverage and slower, self-financed expansion as a choice between fast leveraged growth and resilient growth.

title: The Value of Behavioral Policies
affiliations: University of Chicago - Department of Economics, Bocconi University, Australian National University (ANU) and Washington University in St. Louis

detail.title: The Value of Behavioral Policies
detail.abstract: Behavioral interventions have become central to modern public policy, but their empirical promise remains contested because estimated treatment effects often appear small. We argue that a policy response is economically meaningful only relative to the response generated by alternative policies. We assemble more than 1,200 estimates from over 600 studies comparing "nudges" and traditional price interventions in the markets for cigarettes, alcohol, influenza vaccination, electricity, and residential water. Translating nudge effects into equivalent price changes, we find that behavioral interventions often correspond to enormous fiscal interventions, from an 11% tax on electricity to a 100% subsidy on influenza vaccinations. Nudges are also more cost-effective than price instruments in all markets, but costeffectiveness does not predict the welfare ranking of policies. Using a behavioral extension of the Marginal Value of Public Funds, we show that nudges have high welfare returns at the margin, while price instruments often generate larger total surplus at scale.

title: Binary climate data visuals amplify perceived impact of climate change
affiliations: Carnegie Mellon University, Princeton University, Princeton University - Department of Computer Science and Princeton University

detail.title: Binary climate data visuals amplify perceived impact of climate change
detail.abstract: For much of the global population, climate change appears as a slow, gradual shift in daily weather. This leads many to perceive its impacts as minor and results in apathy (the "boiling frog" effect). How can we convey the urgency of the crisis when its impacts appear so subtle? Here, through a series of large-scale cognitive experiments (N=799), we find that presenting people with binary climate data (e.g., lake freeze history) significantly increases the perceived impact of climate change (Cohen's d = 0.40 [0.26, 0.54]) compared to continuous data (e.g., mean temperature). Computational modeling and follow-up experiments (N=398) suggest that binary data enhances perceived impact by creating an "illusion" of sudden shifts. Crucially, our approach does not involve selective data presentation but rather compares different datasets that reflect equivalent trends in climate change over time. These findings, robustly replicated across multiple experiments, provide a cognitive basis for the "boiling frog" effect and offer a psychologically grounded approach for policymakers and educators to improve climate change communication while maintaining scientific accuracy.

title: Property Rights in Multi-centered Organ Exchange
affiliations: Ozyegin University

detail.title: Property Rights in Multi-centered Organ Exchange
detail.abstract: For patients with organ failure, receiving a deceased-donor transplant is often the only life-saving treatment. Cross-border exchange networks improve matching efficiency by integrating national organ centers, pooling their organ supplies and waiting lists. Because organ centers view their organ supplies as endowments, successful integration hinges on well-defined property rights. We propose three intuitive property-rights axioms and show that Top Trading Cycles is the most promising rule for successful integration, as it uniquely satisfies these axioms. The benchmark nointegration serial rule is inefficient, but we show that it also satisfies certain desirable properties.

title: Making Equity Incentives Actionable: Internal Communication and Broad-Based Employee Ownership
affiliations: Harvard Business School, Harvard Business School and Harvard Business School

detail.title: Making Equity Incentives Actionable: Internal Communication and Broad-Based Employee Ownership
detail.abstract: Broad-based equity compensation gives rank-and-file employees a financial claim on firm value, but it does not clarify how employees should act on that claim. We ask whether communication around an equity plan can clarify these actions and motivate workers. In a field experiment at a building-materials supply company, locations were randomly assigned to receive shareholder letters framing stock appreciation rights around concrete behavioral norms or around abstract organizational values. Norms-based communication reduced turnover by 13.2 percentage points relative to values-based communication and increased employees' self-reported cultural identification. The retention advantage of norms-based communication was concentrated during a period of operational disruption, Hurricane Helene, when behavioral clarity was likely to be especially valuable. A pre-registered online study with construction-sector employees provides controlled evidence consistent with the field patterns, benchmarks norms and values communication against equity-only communication, and identifies message concreteness as the primary measured mechanism. These results suggest that internal communication is a complementary control mechanism that affects the implementation of broad-based equity incentives by clarifying the behaviors through which rank-and-file employees can act on ownership.

title: The Cascade of Inattention: Observability and Responsibility in Vertical Hierarchies

detail.title: The Cascade of Inattention: Observability and Responsibility in Vertical Hierarchies
detail.abstract: A companion working paper-the Equilibrium Without Collusion model (hereafter ewc; SSRN working paper, 2026)-showed that recurring control deficiencies can be an equilibrium without collusion: when a core auditor's observability of a specialist's work is low, declining to understand that work is individually rational, and the deficiency persists with no party deviating and no side payment changing hands. That mechanism turned on a single primitive-accountability is allocated in proportion to what one is seen to be able to observe. This paper nests that primitive vertically and shows that the nesting generates two results the single dyad cannot. In a three-tier hierarchy-executive, manager, employee-each monitoring relationship is an instance of the companion paper's dyad, and the middle player is Janus-faced: observed from above, observer from below. The first result is a cascade of inattention: because the manager's incentive to watch the employee is gated by the executive's watching of the manager, a withdrawal of attention at the top propagates downward-if the executive does not watch the manager, the manager does not watch the employee, and the employee does not work. The executive's watching is precisely what rescues the manager from his own strategic inattention. The second is a two-faced penalty: a heavier penalty on the manager sharpens his discipline of the employee (a structural consequence of the companion paper's attribution premise) while making him less visible to the executive (the companion paper's penalty paradox)-the same comparative static pointing in opposite directions at the two tiers, the net effect set by how much the upward paradox is transmitted back down through the cascade. Both results are established as monotone directions on a code-faithful three-tier model and verified across a grid of detection-curvature and diffuse-penalty values; discontinuities, thresholds, and magnitudes are flagged as functionalform-dependent throughout. A closing section generalizes the frame from a single line to a branching hierarchy, where the same mechanism produces two effects a line cannot: under a binding apex attention budget, disciplined and collapsed divisions coexist within one firmthe firm breaking symmetry even between identical branches-while relative cross-branch evaluation attenuates the coexistence. The audit dyad of the companion paper emerges as the special corner of a general frame in which a monitor has neither credit for nor production stake in the work below-which is why it is the configuration most exposed to the pathology.

title:
Proof-of-Conviction:
A Cryptoeconomic Framework for Type-sorting Token Distribution through Enforced Illiquidity and Continuous-time Screening

detail.title:
Proof-of-Conviction:
A Cryptoeconomic Framework for Type-sorting Token Distribution through Enforced Illiquidity and Continuous-time Screening

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder and sole developer of Streamlock, the protocol whose mechanism is formalized in this paper. The paper describes and analyzes a mechanism designed and implemented by the author.

detail.abstract: Token distribution mechanisms in cryptocurrency markets overwhelmingly rely on immediate resale liquidity (λ = 1), creating an adverse selection environment in which no observable behavior distinguishes high-conviction participants from shorthorizon extractors. This paper introduces a novel primitive: exit timing as a priced signal of conviction. By formalizing the liquidity spectrum λthe fraction of purchased tokens on which the protocol imposes a binding resale restriction at the point of purchasewe show that at λ = 1, token markets exhibit coordination failures consistent with the noise-trader model [De Long et al., 1990] and adverse selection dynamics [Akerlof, 1970], producing a race-to-liquidity in which early exit is individually rational regardless of conviction. Empirical evidence supports these predictions: fewer than 1.4% of tokens on pump.fun graduate to sustained trading, 84.7% of major 2025 token launches trade below their oering price, and buyback programs totaling over $70 million have failed to durably support prices at revenue-generating protocols. We formalize Proof-of-Conviction, a mechanism in which λ = 0 at purchase for all participants and exit is gated by a milestone-dependent state machine (GRIND → FREEZE → UNLOCK) with a linear fee decay from 50% to 1% during unlock windows. The fee schedule transforms exit timing into a priced signal: when a holder exits and how much they pay reveals information about their private valuation. We prove two results that formalize this: non-exiters reveal a lower bound on their reservation value (Theorem 4.1), and exiters reveal a bracketed type interval through their choice of exit time (Corollary 4.2). Together, these results constitute a screening mechanism in the Rothschild & Stiglitz [1976] tradition that produces monotone sorting of holder types through observable behavior. Proof-of-Conviction is presented as a conviction-revealing primitive that any mechanism designer can adopt, not as a complete token distribution system.

title: E-commerce as a Resilience Strategy: Mitigating the impact of COVID-19 on Canada's Agri-Food Trade
affiliations: University of Guelph

detail.title: E-commerce as a Resilience Strategy: Mitigating the impact of COVID-19 on Canada's Agri-Food Trade
detail.abstract: This study investigates the role of the e-commerce infrastructure in mitigating the adverse effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on Canada's agri-food exports. Using a structural gravity model estimated via Poisson pseudo-maximum likelihood (PPML) with monthly data from 2018 to 2022, we assess the resilience-enhancing effect of importer-side e-commerce readiness, while controlling for bilateral tariffs and the multilateral resistance term. Our results show that while COVID-19 indicators on the importer side had limited direct effects, higher levels of e-commerce readiness among Canada's trading partners significantly supported trade continuity. The effects of interaction confirm that the digital infrastructure in Canada's trading partners helped dampen the negative impact of pandemic-related deaths and policy stringency. These findings are robust when we exclude the United States, Canada's dominant trade partner. The study highlights the importance of investing in global digital trade ecosystems and diversifying trade relationships to enhance the resilience and sustainability of Canada's agri-food trade in future crises.

title: Who Signs Matters as Much as What Is Said: Institutional Credibility and Tax Compliance

detail.title: Who Signs Matters as Much as What Is Said: Institutional Credibility and Tax Compliance

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses anonymized administrative records. No individual-level identifying information was used. Ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research uses administrative data provided by the Ministry of Finance of Mexico City. No external funding was received.

detail.abstract: I exploit a large-scale field experiment involving 90,000 delinquent property taxpayers in Mexico City to show that institutional credibility shapes tax compliance independently of message content. The design randomly varies three attributes of reminder letters: message content (deterrence versus tax fairness), signing authority (Fiscal Attorney versus Head of Enforcement Oversight), and whether the signatory's gender is stated explicitly. Holding message content fixed, letters from the Fiscal Attorney-institutionally associated with sanctions-generate significantly higher compliance than identical letters from the Head of Enforcement Oversight. The most effective treatment increases payment probability by 14.7 percentage points over a 2 percent control baseline. Distinguishing response margins is essential: payment probability declines monotonically with accumulated debt, while the number of regularized periods follows an inverted-U, peaking at moderate arrears. Deterrence messages generate larger intensive-margin responses among lower-socioeconomic-status taxpayers, consistent with a sanction-utility channel. These findings imply that enforcement communication is not unidimensional-source credibility, not just message content, affects compliance in ways that standard sender-neutral designs cannot identify.

title: Evidence Without Filtrations Coherent Prevision, Bayes Factors, and the Cross-Filtration Problem
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business, George Mason University and

detail.title: Evidence Without Filtrations Coherent Prevision, Bayes Factors, and the Cross-Filtration Problem
detail.abstract: Safe, anytime-valid inference (SAVI) measures evidence by e-processes: nonnegative processes whose stopped expectation under the null is at most one. Choe and Ramdas (2024) show that an e-process is valid only relative to a filtration. A process valid in a coarse filtration can fail in a finer one, so combining evidence across filtrations needs ad hoc adjusters and pays a logarithmic price. We argue this dependence is an artifact of taking Kolmogorovian adaptedness, not coherent prevision, as primitive. With regular conditional distributions and a Bayes filtration as primitive, the unit of evidence is the predictive Bayes factor, a test martingale under the prior-predictive null by the predictive recursion alone; defined through predictive densities, it transports across filtrations by optional projection. The Choe-Ramdas asymmetry is then the asymmetry of projection: coarsening preserves evidence exactly, while refinement is free precisely when the coarse filtration is immersed in the fine one (H-hypothesis), and the adjuster prices non-immersion. We move beyond martingales (Doob-Meyer, the multiplicative decomposition, the Föllmer measure), give the continuous-time account through the innovations process and the Zakai equation, and identify the betting picture with no-arbitrage: an e-process is a normalized wealth process, Ville's inequality is the statistical fundamental theorem of asset pricing, and the Bayes factor's growth rate is the conditional Kullback-Leibler divergence. We prove the immersion case exactly and conjecture that the adjuster's logarithmic price equals the information surplus of the refinement. A de Finetti reading, the prevision of a prevision (Goldstein, 1983), shows coherence is filtration-free, dissolving the pathology. The motivating example, a manager testing whether returns are random, is Bossaerts's experimental asset-pricing problem, whose efficient-learning resolution is already a predictive martingale in a Bayes filtration.

title: The Great Decoupling: Frontier AI, the Broken Ladder, and the End of the Last Middle Class

detail.title: The Great Decoupling: Frontier AI, the Broken Ladder, and the End of the Last Middle Class

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing personal, financial, or organizational interests that could have influenced this paper. The paper is written in the author’s personal capacity and does not represent the views of any employer, institution, or affiliated organization.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This paper does not involve human participants, patients, personal data collection, interviews, surveys, clinical material, or case-study subjects. It is a conceptual and scenario-analysis working paper based on publicly available academic, policy, market, company, and data sources cited in the references.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this paper.

detail.abstract:
Most macroeconomic and policy frameworks still treat technology as a smooth productivity input and assume that labor markets will eventually clear through gradual re-skilling. This paper argues that Frontier AI, especially in its agentic form, is better understood as a structural break in institutional absorption. The break is no longer confined to model capability. During the first months of 2026, AI moved further into enterprise deployment, professional-service workflows, capital-market repricing, compute infrastructure, and pre-deployment state review. These developments matter because they expose a deeper problem: societies may gain cheaper cognition faster than they can absorb it through labor pipelines, development paths, income distribution, and public legitimacy.

The paper uses scenario analysis rather than point forecasting. It does not claim to identify a single causal effect or predict one inevitable AI future. Instead, it develops a structural-risk framework that maps drivers, transmission channels, vulnerable nodes, early signals, and testable implications. Recent developments in finance agents, legal AI tools, software-market repricing, large compute build-outs, early-career labor-market pressure, and frontier-model testing are treated as signals to be interpreted through this framework, not as final proof of a completed thesis.

The paper makes four contributions. First, it introduces control latency as a scenario-analysis variable, separating deployment latency, verification latency, and distribution latency. Second, it links cognitive-rent compression to professional reproduction failure, especially through the thinning of junior white-collar work. Third, it extends the development debate from AI access to AI absorption, arguing that some countries may be damaged not by exclusion from AI, but by receiving AI before their institutions can absorb the shock. Fourth, it reframes macro-financial stability around income transmission: productivity gains that flow mainly to capital, platforms, model owners, or compute owners do not automatically stabilize household demand.

The central claim is therefore not that AI will simply destroy work. It is that cheaper cognition may arrive into institutions whose stability depended on cognition remaining scarce, socially organized, and wage-bearing. The paper develops this argument through the broken ladder in development, the last middle class in professional labor markets, productivity without broad income transmission, the boundary problem in human-centered institutions, and scenario trajectories for the next phase of AI diffusion. The result is a diagnostic working paper about absorption failure, not a blueprint or a deterministic forecast.

title: Smartphones and Fertility: Evidence From the 2016 4G Rollout in India
affiliations: Stanford University

detail.title: Smartphones and Fertility: Evidence From the 2016 4G Rollout in India
detail.abstract: This paper studies whether smartphone adoption affects fertility. We exploit the nationwide rollout of Reliance Jio's 4G network beginning in September 2016, which dramatically reduced mobile internet costs and accelerated smartphone adoption throughout India. Using multiple waves of the National Family Health Survey (NFHS), we examine whether regions experiencing larger increases in smartphone penetration subsequently experienced larger fertility declines. This paper documents a strong negative relationship between smartphone adoption and fertility both across states and within states over time. To identify causal effects, we exploit variation in exposure to Reliance Jio's rollout generated by pre-existing telecommunications infrastructure and geographic differences in network expansion. This paper further develops an endogenous growth model in which communication technologies increase information access and human capital accumulation while simultaneously reducing fertility. The results contribute to the literature on demographic transition, digital technologies, and long-run economic growth.

title: Evolving Workforce Models in English General Practice: Trends in Consultation Activity and Role Distribution, 2015–2023
affiliations: The Health Foundation, NHS Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit, King’s College London, The Health Foundation, University College London, NHS England, NHS England, NHS Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit, NHS Midlands and Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit, University of Birmingham, The Health Foundation, The Health Foundation, NHS England and The Health Foundation

detail.title: Evolving Workforce Models in English General Practice: Trends in Consultation Activity and Role Distribution, 2015–2023

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The study protocol (reference 23_002752) was reviewed and approved by the Clinical Practice Research Datalink.
declarations.funderStatement: This study was funded by NHS England.

detail.abstract:
Background: General practice in England is undergoing substantial workforce transformation, driven by rising demand, workforce shortages, and policy efforts to broaden and improve multidisciplinary teamworking. Since 2019, the Additional Roles Reimbursement Scheme (ARRS) has supported rapid growth of new clinical and non-clinical roles across Primary Care Networks. However, little is known about how these changes have affected the distribution of consultation activity across staff roles in general practice.

Methods: We conducted a retrospective observational study using CPRD Aurum data from 1,771 English general practices to examine consultation activity between 2015 and 2023. Consultation events were grouped into five staff categories: doctors, nurses, healthcare assistants, healthcare practitioners and ARRS roles. We calculated annual and monthly consultation rates per person-year overall and by deprivation quintile, and used k-means clustering to identify practice-level staffing models.

Findings: Over 140 million patient-years were analysed. Consultation rates fell from 2015 to 2019 before rising sharply during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. The share of consultations delivered by doctors shifted from 62% in 2015 to 52% in 2023, offset by growth in ARRS roles from 2% to 14%. Practices in the most deprived areas had the highest share of consultations delivered by GPs in 2015 and the lowest share in 2023, and saw the largest increases in ARRS and nursing activity. Cluster analysis identified five distinct staffing models, each characterised by comparatively high activity by one staff group.

Interpretation: In the context of rising demand, primary care workforce diversification is reshaping who delivers care in general practice, with notable variation across socioeconomic contexts. While expanding multidisciplinary teams may improve the capacity of general practice to meet patient's needs overall, the fall in GP-led care in deprived areas raises issues about access to care from a doctor for patients who may need it the most.

title: "Navigating Trade Disruptions: Implications for India and Policy Responses"

detail.title: "Navigating Trade Disruptions: Implications for India and Policy Responses"
detail.abstract: The international trading system is experiencing the most significant disruption since the formation of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) in 1948. Five simultaneous shocks have converged to transform the environment in which India must pursue its Viksit Bharat 2047 development vision: the paralysis of the World Trade Organization's Appellate Body since December 2019; sweeping US unilateral tariffs that peaked at 50% on Indian goods before being renegotiated to 18% in February 2026; the European Union's operationalization of its Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) from January 2026; China's accelerating weaponization of rare earth and critical mineral supply chains through export controls covering twelve of the seventeen rare earth elements; and, most acutely, the Strait of Hormuz crisis triggered by US-Israeli military operations against Iran on February 28, 2026, described by the International Energy Agency as the worst energy supply disruption in recorded history. Based on course lectures and session presentations of the International Trade, Business and Policy course, recent external research, and policy responses in recent times, this paper explores the structural aspects of this disruption, evaluates sector-specific implications to India, and details a prioritized, multi-pronged policy response that includes energy security, trade diplomacy, industrial ecosystem development, supply chain resilience, and multilateral reform advocacy.

title: Pricing Compute Futures: Forward Curve and Volatility for a Non-Storable, Depreciating Commodity

detail.title: Pricing Compute Futures: Forward Curve and Volatility for a Non-Storable, Depreciating Commodity
detail.abstract: GPU rental rates are becoming a benchmarked, exchange-traded underlying. In May 2026 CME Group and ICE both announced cash-settled compute futures referencing daily GPU rental indices, with trading expected late 2026. The standard commodity toolkit does not transfer. Compute cannot be stored, so no cash-and-carry relationship anchors the forward curve; the hardware depreciates with each silicon generation, so the curve embeds semi-predictable downward jumps; and spot rates mean-revert toward an equilibrium that is itself bounded below by an energy-linked marginal cost. I propose a tractable framework: a Schwartz-Smith two-factor model extended with a scheduled jump component in which each announced hardware launch window carries a repricing event that is certain to occur but uncertain in size and timing, with options priced via Black-76 on the forward. The model makes three testable predictions ahead of contract launch: structural backwardation as the resting curve shape, a steeply declining volatility term structure, and localized implied-volatility bumps at launch windows, analogous to earnings-date volatility in equity options. The jump magnitude is calibrated to the two completed generational transitions with public price records (the A100 across the H100 ramp; the H100 across the Blackwell ramp); three measurements cluster at -0.22 in log terms (roughly minus 20 percent in price) per event, and realized incumbent depreciation runs 15 to 20 percent per year, well below common intuition. I also examine the basis risk between blended settlement indices and any specific buyer's compute exposure.

title: On the Monotonicity and Concavity of Effective Risk Aversion
affiliations: Shihezi University

detail.title: On the Monotonicity and Concavity of Effective Risk Aversion
detail.abstract: Apparent risk aversion has been extensively studied in the savings problem, but the corresponding portfolio choice object—effective risk aversion, which directly determines the risky portfolio share—has not been characterized for heterogeneous investors. For HARA utility functions with k > 1, apparent prudence is greater than k times apparent risk aversion if and only if the consumption function is concave. Under this condition, effective risk aversion is increasing in wealth if and only if η_t ≤ 1/(φ - 1), where φ denotes the ratio of apparent prudence to apparent risk aversion; a necessary condition, η_t ≤ 1/(k - 1), is shown to always hold. A parallel characterization is obtained for the concavity of effective risk aversion. Furthermore, effective risk aversion approaches zero at the borrowing constraint and 1/(k - 1) as wealth grows without bound. In the special case where apparent prudence equals k times apparent risk aversion, effective risk aversion is always increasing and concave. In the Merton model, the canonical example of this special case, these properties hold whenever income exceeds subsistence consumption.

title: Across the Faultlines: A Multi-Dimensional Index to Measure and Assess Board Diversity
affiliations: Ajman University, Schulich School of Business, York University and Coventry University - Business School

detail.title: Across the Faultlines: A Multi-Dimensional Index to Measure and Assess Board Diversity
detail.abstract: Drawing on faultline theory, this article proposes a multidimensional diversity index (MDI) to measure and assess board diversity. Herein, we contest that diversity needs to be considered across multiple dimensions, or faultlines. Based on the FTSE all-share non-financial firms (2005-2018), the proposed MDI captures the joint effect of differences in director attributes across four faultlines (surface, identity, demographic, and meso-level). After constructing our MDI, we examine how shifts in diversity impact firm risk. Our analysis indicates that moderate levels of diversification (between 0.25 and 0.75) are both typical across our sample and reduce riskiness. At extreme levels of diversification, however, we find that risk increases. We perform further analysis that supports these findings while also showing that, regardless of whether boards are moderately or extremely diversified, their faultline scores are significantly correlated with industry competition and financial risk.

title: Designing Demand Information for a Monopolist Producer
affiliations: University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign, , École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL) and University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign

detail.title: Designing Demand Information for a Monopolist Producer

declarations.funderStatement: Vijeth Hebbar and Cédric Langbort acknowledge funding support from the ARO MURI grant W911NF-20-0252 (76582 NSMUR). Saurabh Vaishampayan and Maryam Kamgarpour acknowledge support from ``UrbanTwin: An urban digital twin for climate action: Assessing policies and solutions for energy, water and infrastructure’’ with the financial support of the ETH-Domain Joint Initiative program in the Strategic Area Energy, Climate and Sustainable Environment. The authors also acknowledge the NCCR Automation Fellowship, which supported Vijeth Hebbar's visit to the Sycamore Lab in 2025, during which this collaboration began.

detail.abstract: Markets with monopolistic producers are susceptible to welfare loss due to economic withholding by producers. To estimate their optimal production quantity, a monopolistic producer needs to estimate the demand curves. In many market setups, the regulator may have access to asymmetric information about the demand. An open question is whether the regulator can strategically reveal demand information to the producer in order to reduce welfare loss. To analyze this, we formulate a Bayesian persuasion problem for the regulator of a market with a homogenous continuous good produced by a monopolist facing an inverse elastic demand curve and a source of stochastic inelastic demand. The regulator designs an information disclosure scheme for the stochastic demand. A core contribution of this work is a tractable characterization of the regulator's optimal disclosure policy. We show that for a broad class of smooth priors, computing the optimal disclosure policy reduces to a scalar convex optimization problem. Furthermore, for producers having nonzero startup costs, the optimal policy pools demand states over a single nonempty interval and reveals truthfully outside of it. We conclude that welfare maximizing regulators can benefit from partial information disclosure.

title: Inflation Learning and Stock Return Dispersion *

detail.title: Inflation Learning and Stock Return Dispersion *
detail.abstract: This paper examines how heterogeneous learning speeds about inflation among investors contribute to cross-sectional variation in stock returns. I develop an asset pricing model in which investors update inflation expectations through Bayesian learning, which leads to persistent belief heterogeneity that impacts firm valuation. The model, supported by an empirical illustration, shows that return differentials widen when learning disparities increase. It further predicts that when slow learners dominate, pricing bias becomes more pronounced even as forecast errors remain limited. These results underscore the role of inflation expectation formation in shaping return dynamics and cross-sectional mispricing.

title: The Taxonomy Trap: AI Paradigm Shifts and the DMA
affiliations: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam

detail.title: The Taxonomy Trap: AI Paradigm Shifts and the DMA
detail.abstract: The Digital Markets Act organizes regulatory obligations around a service-based taxonomy designed for stable intermediation services. Frontier AI systems do not fit that taxonomy. They traverse multiple service categories at once, and faster than the regulatory cycle can track. The result is a mismatch between the obligations the DMA attaches and the conduct it seeks to govern. That mismatch produces miscalibrated enforcement with the potential to distort competition in AI markets.

title: Fragile Intangible Capital: Measuring the Real Cost of Exposed Disinformation
affiliations: Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Donald G. Costello College of Business at George Mason University,  and Southern Methodist University (SMU) - Accounting Department

detail.title: Fragile Intangible Capital: Measuring the Real Cost of Exposed Disinformation

publicationDetails.detailsText: Donald G. Costello College of Business at George Mason University Research Paper (forthcoming)
publicationDetails.journalName: Donald G. Costello College of Business at George Mason University Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: What are the economic consequences when disinformation is exposed? We investigate staggered events where a market information intermediary posts a public alert that a firm's prior reputation has been built around fabricated information-a credibility shock that impairs the firm's belief-based reputational capital without conveying information about products, prices, or physical operations. Exposure of disinformation occurs via two distinct channels-documented evidence of the firm offering compensation in exchange for business reviews and algorithmic detection of suspicious review patterns-each triggering a salient alert to the intermediaries' users. Using the intermediary's algorithm to construct demand-side peer controls based on revealed preferences, and linking each triggering event to GPS foot-traffic and transaction data, we find that exposed firms lose about 8% of foot traffic and 5-6% of transaction volume relative to peers. These losses emerge within a month and persist for at least eighteen months-beyond the removal of public warnings and the end of associated advertising bans-with no sign of recovery. As predicted by our framework, losses scale with reliance on intermediated beliefs-penalties are largest when the exposure of disinformation is backed by clear evidence, during high-demand periods, in areas with deeper intermediary penetration, and for firms more tightly integrated with the intermediary. Exposure also degrades the firm's information environment: ratings decline, review activity falls, and further manipulation is deterred. Fabricated signals boost demand while hidden; their revelation causes lasting demand destruction. Our estimates capture only demand-side effects and exclude any impact on financing costs.

title: Explaining Two Prominent Accounting Pricing Anomalies: The Accrual Anomaly and the Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift
affiliations: and Fanhai International School of Finance(FISF), Fudan University

detail.title: Explaining Two Prominent Accounting Pricing Anomalies: The Accrual Anomaly and the Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift
detail.abstract: The accrual anomaly and the post-earnings-announcement drift (PEAD) are the most prominent pricing irregularities that have called into question the efficiency of the stock market in processing accounting information. Most research documenting the irregularities has benchmarked the returns with expected returns from one-period models. However, investors typically invest over many periods. This paper thus applies a two-factor ICAPM model to explain the anomalies. It finds that returns associated with accruals are rationally pricing the exposures which the multiperiod investor desires. However, PEAD appears to be mispricing which, like momentum pricing, leads the investor into exposures that are inconsistent with rational multiperiod investing. Findings are similar for drifts following revenue surprises and analyst forecast revisions.

title: Shared Data Redundancies and Cyber Attacks
affiliations: Washington University in Saint Louis, John M. Olin Business School

detail.title: Shared Data Redundancies and Cyber Attacks

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This project was initiated jointly with Rodney Garratt. I am grateful for his early input and discussions.

detail.abstract: Redundant data storage safeguards records from cyberattacks, disasters, or negligence. When senders and receivers jointly observe transaction data, redundancy is pairwise: each record is held by exactly two parties. We model data sharing agreements that commit counterparties to restore records after disruptions. Such agreements dominate data autarky but induce free riding and underinvestment in security. We characterize budgetbalanced, state-contingent prices, paid upon recovery, that implement efficient protection and depend on others' investments rather than one's own. We also study a regulated financial infrastructure that can supply an additional security cover but may optimally abstain when it crowds out private protection.

title: War or Media Hype? A Case of AVIC's Stock Gains and Dassault Aviation's Decline during Indo-Pak Tensions 2025
affiliations: Inner Mongolia University of Finance and Economics,  and Woosong University

detail.title: War or Media Hype? A Case of AVIC's Stock Gains and Dassault Aviation's Decline during Indo-Pak Tensions 2025
detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of the recent Indo-Pak conflict on the abnormal returns of firms whose military equipment was used in the assault. This research has employed an event study and TVP-VAR framework to measure abnormal returns and examine their connectedness with a self-developed news media sentiment index and actual war events. The results show negative cumulative abnormal returns for all firms except Avic Chengdu Aircraft (AVIC). The war itself influenced Bharat Dynamics (BDMC), Elbit Systems (ELBT), Hindustan Aeronautics (HINA), and Lockheed Martin (LOCH), while AVIC and Dassault Aviation (DASA) were more reactive to media sentiment. HINA, BDMC, and DASA acted as consistent shock transmitters, with AVIC as a net receiver during and after the war.

title: When Federal Funding Becomes Federal Burden: Program Proliferation and Internal Control Failure Among Nonprofits

detail.title: When Federal Funding Becomes Federal Burden: Program Proliferation and Internal Control Failure Among Nonprofits
detail.abstract: This paper distinguishes federal dollars from federal programs. Dollars expand resources programs expand obligations. In delegated governance, the administrative burden of federal funding is produced not only by how much money flows to organizations, but by how many distinct compliance regimes organizations must manage. Using 4,095 nonprofit entity-years from Minnesota's Single Audit system (FY 2016–2024) and 157,207 program-level federal award records, I find that the cross-sectional association between grant dependence and fewer audit findings (OR = 0.52, p = .001) is not supported by within-entity evidence (entity FE, p = .43),consistent with organizational selection rather than capacity-building. Using program-portfolio expansion during the COVID-era federal funding expansion as identifying variation, I show that nonprofits gaining new federal programs experienced increased audit findings — specifically material weakness (internal control deficiency) — with a lagged entity-FE estimate of +6.2percentage points (p = .001). A falsification test supports the mechanism: entities that gained more dollars without new programs show no finding increase. The effect operates specifically through material weakness — deficiencies in internal controls — rather than through noncompliance or financial distress, consistent with the interpretation that program proliferation overwhelms organizational control infrastructure. IPW-reweighted estimates are attenuated(+4.1pp, p ≈ .10); estimates range from approximately four to seven percentage points across specifications. The findings suggest that when the federal government expands program channels, it may inadvertently increase compliance burden among the organizations it seeks to support.

title: Impact of the China+1 Strategy on India's Export Opportunities and Manufacturing Growth

detail.title: Impact of the China+1 Strategy on India's Export Opportunities and Manufacturing Growth
detail.abstract: Beginning with the U.S. Section 301 tariffs of 2018 and amplified by the pandemic, the Russia-Ukraine war, semiconductor export controls, and the second Trump tariff wave of 2025, multinational firms have systematically been moving incremental manufacturing capacity out of China. The doctrine is called China-Plus-One. India is one of the most-watched candidates to absorb the relocated capacity. This paper asks how well India has actually performed. The empirical record through FY 2024-25 is positive but uneven. Total Indian exports reached a record USD 824.9 billion. Electronics exports rose 32.47 percent in a single year to USD 38.58 billion. Manufacturing FDI grew 18 percent to USD 19.04 billion. India's share of global iPhone production climbed from roughly 1 percent in 2018 to approximately 25 percent by the end of 2025. The pharmaceutical sector turned net exporter of bulk drugs for the first time in over a decade. These are the largest manufacturing-export gains India has registered in a comparable timeframe in its post-independence history. The same dataset, however, reveals real constraints. India's bilateral trade deficit with China widened to USD 99.2 billion in FY 2024-25 and is on track to cross USD 112 billion in FY 2025-26, partly because expanded assembly capacity sucks in Chinese components. Domestic value addition in iPhone manufacturing sits at roughly 19 percent in India, against 40 to 45 percent in China. Logistics costs run at 13 to 14 percent of GDP. India's free-trade-agreement coverage is markedly narrower than Vietnam's or Mexico's. On per-capita FDI inflows, India trails substantially behind Vietnam, Malaysia, Thailand, and Mexico. The China+1 dividend is real, but capturing it fully will require sustained policy work on component-level industry, FTAs, logistics, and skills.

title: The Tacit Dimension of Agentic AI: Relational Competence, Delegated Trust, and the Irreducibly Human Core of High-stakes Interaction

detail.title: The Tacit Dimension of Agentic AI: Relational Competence, Delegated Trust, and the Irreducibly Human Core of High-stakes Interaction

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. This research received no funding and was conducted independently. No personal or financial relationships with any organization influenced this work.

detail.abstract: Agentic AI systems that act autonomously on behalf of human users are being deployed in medical, legal, and financial domains with governance frameworks designed primarily around task competence: accuracy, efficiency, and cost reduction. This paper argues that task competence is a structurally insufficient governance standard for agentic AI in high-stakes human domains, and that two additional competence dimensions-recovery competence and relational competence-are mandatory prerequisites for responsible deployment. We introduce delegated trust failure: the governance gap that emerges when an AI agent acts on a human's behalf, fails, and leaves the human to carry the recovery burden without a pre-built remediation mechanism. We introduce the convenience asymmetry: the systematic divergence between deployer-measured efficiency and user-experienced convenience. And we introduce the tacit knowledge problem: the finding that the most critical professional capability in high-stakes human interaction-what practitioners describe as sensing the vibe, adjusting to the person before asking the first question-is not explicitly definable, not trainable from data, and not certifiable through any current assessment mechanism. Drawing on Polanyi's concept of tacit knowledge and clinical communication research, we propose a three-tier governance framework: task competence for low-stakes automation, recovery competence for consequential transactions, and relational competence for emotionally sensitive high-stakes domains. We argue that in domains where tacit relational knowledge is the critical professional capability, agentic AI should be restricted to administrative functions, with the relational core of the interaction protected as irreducibly human.

title: From the Economics of Choice to the Economics of Human Development: Reconsidering the Economic Agent in the Age of AI

detail.title: From the Economics of Choice to the Economics of Human Development: Reconsidering the Economic Agent in the Age of AI

publicationDetails.detailsText: Behavioral Sustainability and Human-Centered Economics Working Paper Series No.2/2026

detail.abstract: Contemporary economics has produced sophisticated explanations of how individuals choose, but has devoted far less attention to how individuals become capable of choosing meaningfully. This article argues that the dominant analytical traditions in economics, from neoclassical rational choice theory to behavioral economics and human capital theory, remain primarily concerned with decision-making rather than with the formation of the capacities that make meaningful decision-making possible. Against this orientation, the paper advances a development-centered perspective that shifts the object of economic analysis from the act of choice to the formation of the agent who chooses. Building on the capability approach as its normative foundation, this article argues that human development involves not only the expansion of capabilities but also the cultivation of agency, understood as the capacity for purposeful, reflective, and self-directed action. Agency is conceptualized as the bridge between available opportunities and their realization in economic and social life. This article further examines the rise of artificial intelligence as a contemporary stress test for choicecentered economics. As machine systems increasingly perform cognitive tasks at or beyond human competence, the question of what remains distinctive about human economic agency becomes correspondingly urgent. To demonstrate the practical implications of this framework, this article applies it to the case of formal schooling, showing how a development-centered criterion can yield evaluative conclusions that differ from those generated by human capital and capability-based approaches. This article concludes by proposing a development-centered framework in which economic systems are evaluated not only by the opportunities they expand but also by the developmental conditions under which individuals become capable of exercising those opportunities as reflective agents.

title: Quite Booms, Sudden Stops: The Volatility Credit Nexus
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong, The University of Hong Kong and The University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Business and Economics

detail.title: Quite Booms, Sudden Stops: The Volatility Credit Nexus
detail.abstract: Sudden stops are typically preceded by low volatility in both advanced and emerging market economies. Low volatility is an effective predictor of sudden stops, even after controlling for credit and growth. Moreover, a credit boom associated with low volatility is significantly more likely to end in a sudden stop. To account for these facts, we develop a quantitative model with recursive utility, stochastic volatility in productivity trends, and an occasionally binding loan-to-value credit constraint. The model replicates the dynamic patterns among volatility, credit and sudden stops in the data. Low volatility inflates the price of collateral, reduces concerns about a future binding constraint, and encourages borrowing. We show that both recursive preferences and stochastic volatility of trend shocks are essential for the collateral price effect of volatility.

title: Cool by Design: The Hidden Contribution of Coral Sands
affiliations: , Notre Dame University, Louaize and Lebanese University - Faculty of Engineering

detail.title: Cool by Design: The Hidden Contribution of Coral Sands
detail.abstract: Background: Beach quality is a primary determinant of tourist satisfaction and destination loyalty in coastal regions, yet it remains poorly understood and is taken for granted. The physical mechanism by which ecosystem health produces and maintains that quality remains unspecified. We propose that much of this hedonic advantage is grounded in the low thermal conductivity of coral sands, a result of their biogenic origin. This physical property provides a distinctive tactile thermal experience that is a documented driver of tourist satisfaction. It is a direct link between reef ecosystem health and human wellbeing; now quantified, it establishes that the real economic value of coral sands is found "in situ", on the beach. This establishes beach tourism as core pathways for sustainable development and environmental regeneration.

title: Greed Without Programming: How Large Language Models Develop Economic Inequality and Deception Under Survival Pressure

detail.title: Greed Without Programming: How Large Language Models Develop Economic Inequality and Deception Under Survival Pressure
detail.abstract: The world of AI has grown exponentially and their behavior is being heavily studied. We see deception occurring everyday in humans, but how would an LLM deceive? By running 6 agents in 7 models with 50 rounds each and 4 different resources in a closed economy we are able to track how LLMs are able to deceive, interact, and compete with each other to try and end up on top. Findings show an average deception rate of around 97.23% showing these models will use deception to its highest capacity and strategically at that. Another factor calculated was the Gini coefficient ranging from around 0.085 to 0.248 it displays a significant wealth imbalance being present. Additionally there was a 192% inequality difference from swapping models showing that a smarter more powerful model is likely to induce more inequality between LLMs. Something to keep in mind however is the LLMs were not prompted to deceive each other, rather it was a survival tactic used deceiving others to gain the upper hand with the models. This induces an institutional question, who shall be held responsible for LLM deception, the company making it, the one using it or the AI itself?

title: The Origins of Inequality in Mean-Field Economies: A Pareto-Tail Decomposition

detail.title: The Origins of Inequality in Mean-Field Economies: A Pareto-Tail Decomposition
detail.abstract: We develop a tractable continuous-time heterogeneous-agent framework for analyzing Pareto upper-tail wealth inequality. The stationary wealth distribution admits a Pareto upper tail under asymptotically linear drift and multiplicative diffusion. With type heterogeneity, each type generates its own tail exponent, and the aggregate upper tail is governed by the tail-dominating type. We decompose the equilibrium Pareto exponent into preference-related heterogeneity, risk-related heterogeneity, and general-equilibrium feedback. A stylized quantitative illustration shows how these channels shape upper-tail concentration. The decomposition is then given a responsibility-sensitive interpretation in terms of choice, circumstance, and equilibrium amplification.

title: Dynamic Capital Input, Liquidity Management and Hedging with Data-Driven Productivity
affiliations: Hunan University - School of Finance and Statistics, Hunan University - School of Finance and Statistics and Jishou University

detail.title: Dynamic Capital Input, Liquidity Management and Hedging with Data-Driven Productivity
detail.abstract: We develop a continuous-time model of a financially constrained firm where data is a key input jointly determining firm value, capital input, financing, liquidity management and hedging. We find that data intensity increases firm value and marginal q of data, while inducing higher cash holdings. Moreover, a higher data intensity reduces capital input, which leads to lower data growth under tight liquidity but enhances it when ample internal liquidity strengthens the data feedback loop. Under time-varying conditions, the effects of data intensity are strongly state-dependent, higher data intensity raises refinancing issuance boundary and widens the wedge between capital input and data growth rate. Finally, greater data intensity strengthens hedging incentives. With refinancing access, higher data intensity leads the firm to speculate earlier at lower cash levels while increasing hedge ratio when cash holdings are high. Our results are also consistent with some empirical evidence.

title: Mixed-Frequency Impulse Responses
affiliations: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Department of Economics and Universidad de San Andres

detail.title: Mixed-Frequency Impulse Responses
detail.abstract: We show that temporal aggregation of variables to a common frequency introduces identification failures that cannot be resolved by standard methods. When the outcome variable is observed at a lower frequency than the shock of interest, aggregation distorts the mapping from structural shocks to reduced-form innovations. As a result, none of the leading identification strategies recover the true impulse responses from an aggregated model. We propose a mixed-frequency approach that preserves the high-frequency variation in the shock. Under this approach, all the traditional identification strategies remain valid, either when identification relies on external instruments or when it is achieved through assumptions internal to the model.

title: Dynamic Capital Input, Liquidity Management and Hedging with Data-Driven Productivity

detail.title: Dynamic Capital Input, Liquidity Management and Hedging with Data-Driven Productivity
detail.abstract: We develop a continuous-time model of a financially constrained firm where data is a key input jointly determining firm value, capital input, financing, liquidity management and hedging. We find that data intensity increases firm value and marginal q of data, while inducing higher cash holdings. Moreover, a higher data intensity reduces capital input, which leads to lower data growth under tight liquidity but enhances it when ample internal liquidity strengthens the data feedback loop. Under time-varying conditions, the effects of data intensity are strongly state-dependent, higher data intensity raises refinancing issuance boundary and widens the wedge between capital input and data growth rate. Finally, greater data intensity strengthens hedging incentives. With refinancing access, higher data intensity leads the firm to speculate earlier at lower cash levels while increasing hedge ratio when cash holdings are high. Our results are also consistent with some empirical evidence.

title: Infinite Horizon Optimal Consumption: Intertemporal Hedging under Epstein-Zin Preferences
affiliations: University of Michigan at Ann Arbor and University of Michigan at Ann Arbor - Department of Mathematics

detail.title: Infinite Horizon Optimal Consumption: Intertemporal Hedging under Epstein-Zin Preferences
detail.abstract: We study an infinite-horizon optimal consumption-investment problem for an investor with Epstein-Zin stochastic differential utility with stochastic investment opportunities in an incomplete market. Risk aversion and intertemporal substitution are separated, and we work in the regime θ ∈ (0, 1), where there exists a unique generalised utility process for arbitrary non-negative progressively measurable consumption streams. Our main contribution is a variational characterisation of the value function. We show that the value function is the unique minimiser of a functional whose Euler-Lagrange equation coincides with the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation. Although the functional may be non-convex, the direct method yields existence, and we prove every minimiser is strictly positive, bounded, and classical. A verification theorem identifies any minimiser with the value function and gives feedback representations for optimal consumption and investment policies. The proof combines a change of measure to the myopic probability with uniqueness results for Epstein-Zin BSDEs and a perturbation argument for optimality. Examples with stochastic volatility, Gaussian excess returns, and fat-tailed excess returns illustrate the scope of the framework and its implications for intertemporal hedging.

title: Residual-Personalized Ensemble Learning for Short-Term Weight Change and Rebound Risk Prediction in Mobile Health Systems

detail.title: Residual-Personalized Ensemble Learning for Short-Term Weight Change and Rebound Risk Prediction in Mobile Health Systems
detail.abstract: ​Accurate short-term forecasting of body-weight dynamics remains challenging in personalized digital health systems due to substantial inter-individual variability in physiological responses to exercise. This study proposes a residual-personalized ensemble learning framework for 30-day weight change and rebound-risk prediction using multimodal behavioral and anthropometric data. Rolling-window aggregation captures short-term training dynamics, while dual-domain clustering characterizes physiological profiles (BodyCluster) and behavioral running patterns (RunCluster). A personalized baseline weight-change slope is estimated for each user, and residual deviations from this trend are modeled to reduce inter-individual bias. The framework integrates ensemble regressors and sequential deep learning models, alongside logistic classifiers for weight-loss and rebound-risk detection. Experimental results show that residual personalization improves generalization compared with direct forecasting. Tree-based ensembles achieve MAE ≈ 0.9 kg and R² ≈ 0.72, while rebound-risk classification reaches F1 > 0.70. Cluster-association analysis (Cramér’s V ≈ 0.30) indicates moderate coupling between anthropometric structure and behavioral patterns. The proposed framework provides an interpretable and deployment-ready solution for individualized short-term weight forecasting in mobile health systems.

detail.abstract: This paper studies decision problems in which an opportunity is available but its temporal origin is unknown. In such settings, continued availability is informative: an opportunity that survives long enough to be observed is selected by the behavior, inaction, or absence of prior agents. This mechanism is called retrospective informational selection. The paper formalizes this idea using a first-buyer problem in which a prize is awarded to the first agent who purchases a costly ticket, while agents are uncertain about the opportunity's age and the arrival process of prior agents. In a Poisson-arrival model, the probability of being first is given by the Laplace transform of the prior distribution over opportunity age, evaluated at the product of the arrival rate and the prior-agent purchase probability. Three results characterize the equilibrium: the purchase condition is given by the Laplace transform of the age prior; the symmetric equilibrium involves either immediate purchase or a unique interior mixed equilibrium; and the equilibrium purchase probability increases in the prize, decreases in the ticket cost, and decreases in the arrival rate of prior agents. Together, these results show that first-mover incentives depend not only on the prize-to-cost ratio but also on beliefs about the opportunity's unobserved temporal history. The framework links timing, informational inference, and strategic reasoning about prior agents, and it yields implications for how decision-makers interpret continued availability.

title: Morphometric Prediction of Body Weight in Kuri Cattle: Validation of Published Equations for Sub-Saharan African Taurine Breeds and Analysis of Determinants of Predictive Performance​

detail.title: Morphometric Prediction of Body Weight in Kuri Cattle: Validation of Published Equations for Sub-Saharan African Taurine Breeds and Analysis of Determinants of Predictive Performance​
detail.abstract: Accurate estimation of body weight in cattle remains a major challenge in African extensive livestock systems, where access to weighing equipment is often limited. This study, conducted on 289 Kuri  cattle reared in the Diffa region of Niger, aimed to assess the predictive performance of 61 morphometric equations previously developed for sub-Saharan African taurine breeds and to develop breed-specific models tailored to Kuri  cattle. Data collected included body weight, heart girth, height at withers, and body length. The newly developed models were evaluated using repeated cross-validation (10-fold, 5 repetitions), together with independent intra-breed and cross-sex external validation. Model performance was assessed using Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Lin’s Concordance Correlation Coefficient (CCC), prediction bias, calibration slopes, and decomposition of mean squared error. The results showed that only 6% of the published equations achieved excellent predictive performance, whereas approximately 58% exhibited poor transferability to the Kuri  population, with prediction errors occasionally exceeding 20–50%. The predictive accuracy of published equations was significantly influenced by production system, breed, and physiological category of the animals, highlighting the substantial impact of biological and zootechnical context on equation robustness. Locally developed models consistently outperformed the generic African equations. The multilinear model incorporating heart girth and body length (BW = −583 + 4.0HG + 2.7BL) demonstrated the highest predictive performance (CCC = 0.86; RMSE = 8.15%), together with excellent stability during external validation procedures (CCC reaching 0.97 in males). These findings underscore the importance of developing and rigorously validating population-specific equations to improve body weight estimation in African livestock production systems.
